stories.title: Week 2 Aftermath: Anthony Edwards, Kawhi Leonard and others join the dreaded injury list
stories.summary: The Timberwolves, Pacers and Raptors are among the teams that have to account for star players being sidelined for extended periods after Week 2.
stories.detailText: For all of us who hoped that we were done with major injuries impacting the NBA and fantasy basketball after a rough opening week, Week 2 was disappointing. Oklahoma City saw another starter join the long list of important players sidelined for extended periods, while Minnesota and Indiana lost their respective offensive focal points to lower-body injuries. Let's take a look back at Week 2, starting with the Timberwolves. Fantasy Basketball Weekend Streamers: Ja’Kobe Walter, Tristan da Silva starring as injury replacements Ja’Kobe Walter and Tristan da Silva lead a group of 10 players worth streaming this weekend. Noah Rubin , Five Week 2 Storylines - Anthony Edwards to miss at least two months: Edwards' right knee had been an issue for the star guard going back to last season's playoffs, and he was dealing with soreness going into Monday's game against the Cavaliers. While he managed 47 points in the overtime defeat, fantasy managers got terrible news afterward. Edwards would have to undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his knee (this occurred on Thursday) and miss at least two months. Ayo Dosunmu has moved into the starting lineup, and as many fantasy managers hoped, his production has increased. In three starts, the Timberwolves guard has averaged 19.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 2.3 steals and 2.7 three-pointers, shooting 57.5 percent from the field and 100 percent from the foul line. Edwards' absence also means the Timberwolves will need more production from Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga , and more consistency out of LaMelo Ball . Ball's 24-point, seven-assist showing in an October 30 win over the Clippers was sandwiched in between disappointing outings against the Warriors and Spurs. In those defeats, Ball totaled 18 points, 12 assists and 11 turnovers, shooting 5-of-21 from the field and 2-of-12 from three. Given Edwards' expected return timeline, the Timberwolves can't afford extended stretches of inconsistent production from Ball. - Thunder lose Chet Holmgren for at least 8-10 weeks: Already without Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) and Cason Wallace (shoulder), the Thunder lost Holmgren to a partially torn patellar tendon. He'll be out for at least 8-10 weeks, leaving Oklahoma City down three starters. Kenrich Williams has started the last three games, most recently finishing an October 31 loss to the Rockets with 11 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers. In those starts, he's played 24, 17 and 21 minutes, so the fantasy upside may be limited. Holmgren's absence also means the Thunder will need more production from rookie Aday Mara . Over the last three games, he has averaged 8.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.7 blocks per game, shooting 52.9 percent from the field and 85.7 percent from the foul line. Williams may bring three-point production, but Mara is the better option for managers who need rebounds and blocks. One question is how the absences will affect Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , since there are fewer proven scorers around him. He's shot 49.1 percent from the field over the last three games, averaging 24.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.7 three-pointers per game during this stretch. While he should remain one of the top players in fantasy basketball, his efficiency could take a hit due to the absences of Holmgren, J-Dub, and Wallace. - Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton suffers a strained hamstring: After missing the entire 2025-26 season rehabbing from a ruptured Achilles tendon suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, Haliburton got off to an excellent start this season. Unfortunately, he's joined the long list of injured stars, as a hamstring strain suffered during Monday's loss to the Bucks has sidelined Haliburton for an undetermined amount of time. Andrew Nembhard , who has been dealing with a sore neck, has become the lone point guard in the Pacers' starting lineup, while Kelly Oubre Jr. has been the fifth starter. He shot 13-of-32 in losses to the 76ers and Heat, but Nembhard totaled 40 points and 23 assists while committing six turnovers. Most fantasy managers will take that production from Nembhard, especially with him shooting 47.5 percent from the field this season. Indiana has also been without starting center Ivica Zubac, who sprained his ankle on October 25 against the Nets. Jay Huff has started each of the last three games, totaling 22 points, 13 rebounds and four three-pointers. However, he has not recorded a steal or blocked shot in those starts. As long as he's healthy, Obi Toppin may be a better streaming option than Huff despite coming off the bench. Toppin did not play against the Heat on Friday, but he totaled 27 points, 12 rebounds, and three three-pointers in Indiana's first two games of the week. - Ja Morant expected to miss at least four weeks: Morant's start with the Trail Blazers was going smoothly until he suffered a strained hamstring during Thursday's loss to the Grizzlies. He's expected to miss at least four weeks with what was determined to be a Grade 2 strain. Scoot Henderson started Saturday's win over the Jazz, finishing with 14 points, three rebounds, one assist, three steals and one three-pointer, shooting 4-of-11 from the field and committing four turnovers. Efficiency has long been a concern regarding Henderson, but the opportunity to start makes him an intriguing option for fantasy managers needing to account for Morant's injury. That said, this injury also means more will be asked of Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija , both of whom are already rostered in over 96 percent of Yahoo leagues. Jrue Holiday recorded a solid stat line against the Jazz and is still available in some 12-team leagues. He played 22 minutes on Saturday, with his time limited by Portland's 22-point win. - Kawhi Leonard expected to miss 3-4 weeks: Leonard has been out since Toronto's October 25 loss to the Timberwolves, and he's going to be out for a while longer as he deals with a knee issue. The Raptors announced on October 29 that he's expected to miss 3-4 weeks, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Ja'Kobe Walter . After scoring 22 points against Minnesota, he totaled 23 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and six three-pointers in two games against the Magic. Also of note was Scottie Barnes ' play after going scoreless on 0-of-12 shooting against Minnesota. Against the Magic, he attempted 51 shots in the two games (making 30) and totaled 69 points, 11 rebounds, nine assists, five steals and two blocks. While Walter has become a worthy streamer while Leonard sits, fantasy managers who are rostering Barnes may benefit. Five More Storylines - Will there come a point this season when the Pelicans hand Jeremiah Fears the keys: The Pelicans began the season starting Fears and Dejounte Murray alongside each other, which likely played a role in the second-year guard's limited production in the first four games. Fears averaged just 9.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 three-pointers per game while shooting 31.1 percent from the field. Murray has missed the last two games for personal reasons, and Fears' numbers have skyrocketed. His averages in wins over the Kings and Hawks: 21.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, 10.0 assists, 1.5 steals, 2.0 blocks and 2.0 three-pointers, shooting 64.3% from the field. With Murray in the final guaranteed year of his current contract (he has a player option for 2027-28 worth just over $30.7 million), will there come a point when the Pelicans simply hand Fears the keys to the offense? He and Derik Queen were the franchise's two 2025 first-round picks, and you would assume giving them every opportunity to prove themselves would be a priority. We'll see, but the front office must have been thrilled with what they saw from Fears in the last two games. - AJ Dybantsa makes his official Wizards debut: Back from a sprained ankle suffered during the Wizards' preseason finale, Dybantsa debuted as a starter in Wednesday's loss to the Cavaliers. In two games, the rookie averaged 18.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists while shooting 13-of-23 from the field. Dybantsa played 27 minutes against Cleveland and 29 against Charlotte, with the Wizards taking a measured approach to his playing time. AJ's return pushed Bilal Coulibaly to the bench, and after scoring 17 points against the Cavaliers, he scored just one against the Hornets. - Jabari Smith Jr. may be taking the next step in Houston: While solid for most of his first four NBA seasons, Smith tended to leave people wanting more, given his physical gifts. Now may be the time for the fifth-year forward, whose improved production is one reason the Rockets are 6-7. Through seven games, Smith has averaged 19.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 0.9 steals, 0.9 blocks and 3.0 three-pointers, shooting 48.9 percent from the field and 88% from the foul line. While his rebounding has dipped, Smith's scoring is up more than three points per game, and the assists and three-pointers would also be career-best averages if they held. Most recently, he recorded 30 points, nine rebounds, five assists, one block and six three-pointers in Saturday's win over the Thunder. - Spurs taking a methodical approach to Tobias Harris' rehab: Prior to the Spurs' Halloween night win over the Timberwolves, Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said that the team was acting “very, very methodically” regarding Harris' recovery from the calf strain he suffered during the preseason. The veteran forward, who agreed to a two-year deal with the Spurs in July, has no timeline for a return to the court. Will the starting lineup, which currently includes three guards ( De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper ), be up for discussion once Harris is healthy? We'll see, but that doesn't seem like something fantasy managers will need to worry about anytime soon. - Suns plan to stick with Jalen Green as a starter: Green's gotten off to a very slow start, averaging 11.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.0 three-pointers per game in four appearances. Phoenix dropped to 1-3 after its loss to the Nuggets on Friday, and questions arose about Green's fit in the starting lineup after he finished with two points. However, Suns head coach Jordan Ott and guard Collin Gillespie , the logical replacement if Phoenix makes a change, both backed Green after the defeat. Keep an eye on that situation as the season progresses, especially if the Suns keep struggling. Three Questions 1. Should fantasy managers be concerned with Nikola Jokić's scoring average decreasing by over six points compared to last season? 2. Will the Thunder look to use some of their draft capital to strengthen the roster? 3. Can the Grizzlies get to 9-0? He made 17, finishing with 43 points, seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, six blocks and three three-pointers. The Timberwolves were without Rudy Gobert (back), leaving second-year center Joan Beringer to defend Wemby. 51: Heat center Bam Adebayo totaled 51 points in Miami's last two games of the week, comfortable wins over the Hawks and Pacers. He was also responsible for 18 rebounds, six assists and six steals while shooting 19-of-30 from the field. After a rough start, the partnership between Bam and Giannis Antetokounmpo appeared to have gotten stronger in those victories. 49: Lakers star Luka Dončić has attempted 49 three-pointers over his last three games, making 20. That stretch began with a 52-point effort against the Jazz on October 25, and he's scored at least 37 points in all three games. Could Luka wind up being more valuable than SGA or Nikola Jokić this season? stories.title: Dusty May is exactly what the city of Dallas needed
stories.summary: The first-year head coach already has a hold on the hearts of Mavericks fans.
stories.detailText: It has been a long 19 months since Luka Doncic was traded. It has been an even longer 29 months since Mavericks fans were riding the high of making the NBA Finals and looking forward to the next 10 years of competition. At the time of the trade, it was hard to see how Dallas would ever recover from it. I, personally, could not see a world in which I would feel joy watching the Mavericks for the foreseeable future. Then, Dallas lucked into Cooper Flagg. His rookie year was enjoyable, but so many remnants of the previous year remained. They had to fire the man who made the trade. Then, they had to trade the guy they received in the Doncic deal. Eventually, they made the decision to move on from the coach who oversaw all of these things when a new regime was put in place. And then Dusty May was hired, and he gave the city of Dallas something that was long overdue: a hope for joy again. If you live in Dallas, you know how the city felt in the spring of 2025: sad, lifeless, and hurting. Yes, it’s true that the DFW metroplex is a football town, but the Cowboys play in Arlington (and are perpetually disappointing), which is 30-45 minutes away. So does the baseball team, the Rangers, which means Dallas proper feels most alive when the Mavericks are good. For over a year and a half, things felt off. Conversations that used to be had about the Mavericks were silent, buzz downtown on game days was non-existent, and the anticipation of playoff basketball was years down the road. There was still a long way to go to get back to where it felt the fan base was two years ago. Even with Flagg as the future, there was still some skepticism regarding how the team would rebound. But when basketball started less than two weeks ago, those worries started to melt away. The Mavs are finally making us feel basketball feelings again. When I went to the Mavericks’ game on Friday night versus the Rockets, the arena felt like it did once upon a time. The city and people around me felt alive again, and Mavericks’ forward Naji Marshall seemed to notice the same thing: AAC back to blowing the roof off wowwwww top 5 feeling 😭… — Naji Marshall (@marshall_naji8) October 31, 2026 But what changed? This team is, in large part, the same as last season. Well, like I said before, the final step to moving on was getting a new coach. May has been a breath of fresh air. He is always smiling; he emits joy whenever he talks. He is personable in a way that Jason Kidd simply was not. He is constantly talking up his guys and praising them when they play well. He is, for all intents and purposes, the antithesis of everything that happened before he was hired. The team even plays like an extension of him. They root for each other, they gang rebound, they have fun playing passing the ball, and, most of all, they play for the city of Dallas. May even said it himself when talking about the synergy between the coaches and front office : “We’re all working together.”, May said. “We’re trying to represent this city the best way possible. And we’re all trying to achieve the same thing – to improve on and off the court because ultimately the way we play on the floor brings enjoyment to people’s lives.” And that last point, about bringing enjoyment to people’s lives, is the key element that previous decision-makers in the organization failed to realize. Dallas is full of hardworking people. Thousands of Mavericks fans clock in at 9:00 AM with the hope that after a beer or two and a Mavericks tipoff at 7:00 PM, the stresses of daily life will become a little easier. Sometimes that two-and-a-half-hour basketball game is all you need to decompress after a long day. That’s why Dallas rooted so hard for Doncic. He played with a joy that you could see reflected in the city. He was a release valve for the everyday fan. When he was dealt away, that joy he created faded quickly. But May understands that. He knows what Dallas has been through. And not only does he want his team to win, but he wants to bring the whole city with them. And he makes that clear with everything he does. Sometimes it is hard to see the effect that a coach has on a team. But with May, that effect not only is evident in the basketball product, but it reverberates throughout the entire Dallas area. Flagg gave Mavericks fans hope again; May brought back our joy.

stories.title: A look at the Suns’ schedule for November
stories.summary: How does the calendar shape up for the first full month of the season?
stories.detailText: Oct 30, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Phoenix Suns forward Miles Bridges (22) goes up for a layup against Denver Nuggets forward Trevon Brazile (7) during the second half at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Despite playing the fewest games in the NBA during the inaugural month of the season, concern is high among the Phoenix Suns fanbase due to their offensive struggles and lack of a point guard in the starting lineup amid their 1-3 start. Fans will remain concerned about their season outlook until they start to string a win streak together and play more cohesively. They’ll have a few opportunities to do so throughout the first whole month of the NBA season. Here’s a peek at the Suns’ schedule for November. The longest homestand since COVID Monday , November 2nd @ Golden State Warriors Wednesday, November 4th vs Portland Trail Blazers Thursday, November 5th vs Orlando Magic Saturday, November 7th vs Houston Rockets Monday, November 9th vs San Antonio Spurs Tuesday, November 10th vs Los Angeles Clippers Thursday, November 12th vs Charlotte Hornets Sunday, November 15th vs Los Angeles Lakers After their Monday matchup in San Francisco against the Warriors, Phoenix will have their longest homestand since February of the 2020-2021 season, when the schedule was made to limit travel during the pandemic. A mix of games against the Eastern and Western Conferences, the Suns were .500 or better against all of their upcoming home opponents except for the Rockets last season. With multiple back-to-backs in the homestand, the Suns will need to make sure they play a balanced and deep lineup, but the lack of travel will give the team more time to rest between games. A homestand ends and a road trip begins Monday, November 16th @ Denver Nuggets Wednesday, November 18th @ Sacramento Kings Friday, November 20th @ Utah Jazz * Monday, November 23rd @ New Orleans Pelicans Wednesday, November 25th @ Houston Rockets * (*=NBA Cup Games) The five-game road trip is tied for the longest road trip the Suns will have all year, and the start of it will provide Phoenix with an opportunity for revenge against the Nuggets, who handed them their most recent loss. One of the two winless teams left, the Kings project to provide Phoenix with one of their easiest games of the year, before they play in two of three NBA Cup Games to finish out their travels, with the game against Houston being Jalen Green’s first game at the Toyota Center since being traded for Kevin Durant in 2025. He missed both games in Houston last year because of hamstring issues. Post-Thanksgiving clashes with rising stars Friday, November 27th vs Dallas Mavericks * Sunday, November 29th @ Utah Jazz (*=NBA Cup Games) After a break for Thanksgiving, Phoenix will face off against Cooper Flagg and Darryn Peterson, the first and second picks in the 2025 and 2026 drafts. While Peterson has struggled mightily with efficiency to start his career, Flagg has been an offensive and defensive force, leading the Mavericks to a surprising 4-2 start and handing the Rockets their first loss of the season after their 5-0 start behind his 33-point performance. The games against the young talent will give the Suns a glimpse at what life could have been like if they opted to rebuild and accumulate assets after their 2022 and 2023 playoff shortcomings rather than go all-in on acquiring Bradley Beal, which stripped them of all their remaining draft capital after trading for Kevin Durant months prior. How do you think the Suns will fare in November?

stories.title: Celtics will be without key starter when they face Magic
stories.summary: Robinson will miss his first game of the season as the Celtics rest him on the front-end of a back-to-back.
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 30: Joe Mazzulla of the Boston Celtics high-fives Mitchell Robinson #4 during the first half against the Chicago Bulls at the TD Garden on October 30, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Celtics will be without Mitchell Robinson when they face the Orlando Magic. Robinson will rest on the front end of a back-to-back, the Celtics’ second of the season. So far this season, Robinson has averaged 6.6 points and 4.6 rebounds in 20 minutes per game. The rest of the roster, except two-way player Devin Carter, is fully available. Carter continues to deal with an illness, though he is now around the team after being away to start the season. Robinson typically did not play in both nights of back-to-backs as a member of the New York Knicks, but in an interview with Knicks Fan TV earlier this month, he made clear that would not be the case in Boston. ”It ain’t going to be the same in Boston [as it was with the Knicks]. I’ll be able to play back-to-backs,” Robinson said. “I’m very excited for that; it’s been a long time coming. Now I can go out there and play basketball, just go out there with a free mind and just hoop.” The Celtics are 4-1 entering Sunday’s game, while the Magic are 2-3, with wins over the New York Knicks and Toronto Raptors and losses to the Atlanta Hawks, Minnesota Timberwolves, and the Raptors. Boston has won four straight since losing the season opener, beating the Knicks, Chicago Bulls (twice), and Brooklyn Nets. The Magic will be without several key players Paolo Banchero suffered a high ankle sprain in the second game of the season, while Jalen Suggs suffered a right knee contusion in the third. Jonathan Isaac is out with left knee injury management. Franz Wagner has led the Magic, averaging 20.8 points, 7 assists, and 6.8 rebounds per game. Desmond Bane, acquired last offseason, averages 17.2 points, 4 rebounds, and 2.8 assists. Wendell Carter Jr. is having a career season so far, averaging 14.8 points and 8.6 rebounds. And in the wake of injuries, Anthony Black and Jase Richardson have slotted into the starting lineup, with Jamal Cain and Tristan da Silva playing key minutes off the bench. Neemias Queta is likely to get the start for Boston The Celtics have started Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, and Robinson every game so far this season. With Robinson out, Neemias Queta will likely slot into the starting lineup, and Luka Garza will see more minutes off the bench. Queta is averaging 9 points and 4.8 rebounds in 19.8 minutes per game for the Celtics so far. Garza is averaging 4.6 points and 2.2 rebounds in 8.8 minutes per game. The Celtics may rest players for Monday’s game against the Houston Rockets, but the entire rotation played in both games when the team last had a back-to-back. Celtics-Magic tips off at 3:30pm ET at the Kia Center in Orlando.

The Brooklyn Nets opened NBA Cup play with a Friday night matchup against the Detroit Pistons. Brooklyn got off to a great start and looked like they were going to give last year’s top seed in the Eastern Conference a good fight. Unfortunately for the home fans, they watched the Nets suffer another blowout. Brooklyn let things slip in the middle of the game and lost 110-94 . They’re now sitting at 0-5 to begin the season — one of two remaining winless teams (Kings). The opponent tonight projects to be a contender for the NBA Championship. That is, if everyone is healthy. The Indiana Pacers are hoping to get back to the NBA Finals after missing out last season. It’s early, but the road back to the postseason has been a rocky one. They were on the road Friday night against the new look Miami Heat and lost 144-125. Game Info and Broadcast Details Matchup : Brooklyn Nets (0-5) vs. Indiana Pacers (2-4) Time : 5 PM EST (4 PM CST) Location : Gainbridge Fieldhouse (Indianapolis, Indiana) TV/Streaming : YES Network, WFAN Radio, DAZN Nets-Pacers Injury Report: Who’s Out? Brooklyn Nets OUT – Egor Demin (right bone bruise) OUT – Mikel Brown Jr (back injury management) OUT – Joshua Jefferson (G League assignment) OUT – Ben Saraf (G League assignment) OUT – Tyler Bilodeau (G League tw0-way) OUT – Grant Nelson (G League two-way) Indiana Pacers OUT – Tyrese Haliburton (left hamstring strain) OUT – Ben Sheppard (left meniscus surgery) OUT – Ivica Zubac (left ankle sprain) OUT – Johnny Furphy (right ACL surgery) OUT – T.J. McConnell (right hamstring strain) Probable – Aaron Nesmith (left hamstring strain) Questionable – Obi Toppin (low back soreness) The Game Indiana won the first meeting 136-109 on October 25. This is the first leg of a back-to-back for the Nets. They return to the city for a matchup against the New York Knicks on Monday night at the Garden. The Nets are off to their worst possible start, and Friday’s loss to Detroit didn’t do much to inspire confidence. People can accept losing, but they can’t accept poor effort. Brooklyn’s latest defeat left plenty of questions about the team’s effort and execution. This year was supposed to be different for the Nets, but it looks all too familiar. Nolan Traore will get all the minutes he can handle tonight. With Demin and Brown Jr out, it’s on him to man the point. That’s a lot on his shoulders. He’ll need to dictate the offense and generate downhill pressure. If he does get to the rim, the Nets need him to turn those opportunities into points. In October, the Nets were dead last in the NBA in field goal percentage inside the restricted area at 55.2 percent. That’s a troubling number against a Pacers team that has allowed opponents to shoot just 60.2 percent inside the restricted area, the third-best mark in the league. The home team need something to break their way, and if they want to finally break into the win column, it’ll take a total team effort. Maybe the new month is what the doctor ordered? Andrew Nembhard is probably never going to make an All-Star Game, but he’s someone I’d love to have on my side. He’s someone you can trust to make something happen with the game on the line. He’s also become more efficient while taking on a bigger offensive role. Brooklyn will have its hands full with the speedy guard, who’s averaging 17.6 points and eight assists per game. Player to Watch: Pascal Siakam Siakam has been one of the better forwards in the NBA in the 2020s. He’s done well in his various roles and can scale his scoring up when the moment calls for it. He’s been turning the ball over at a career-high clip to start the year, but that is something to monitor as Indiana navigates the early part of its schedule. Without Haliburton, the four-time All-Star will have to up his game and take on more of the scoring load to offset the absence of their franchise player. Brooklyn also needs more from Julius Randle. He discussed the process on offense after Friday’s game, and he shared some interesting insights about what the Nets need to improve: Asked Julius Randle about the Nets' offensive struggles: “There’s no flow and rhythm after this after the first action… It's like sometimes we get bogged down or stuck, and we're just sitting there watching each other, and it's not putting us in the best position to succeed.… pic.twitter.com/qKmLd2kFqx — Erik Slater (@ErikSlater_) October 31, 2026 Brooklyn has to find their purpose, and fast. If the team can’t play with more pace and with more success at the rim, a long season is guaranteed to get even longer. stories.title: Tyler Kolek's strong start gives the Knicks a tough rotation decision when Jose Alvarado returns
stories.summary: Despite the end of his turnover-free streak, Tyler Kolek continues to impress, giving the Knicks a tough choice in their crowded backcourt.
stories.detailText: All good streaks are supposed to come to an end. In Friday's 98-93 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers, Knicks guard Tyler Kolek 's stretch of perfection ended. In the game's early stages, he turned the ball over for the first time this season. Kolek coughed up the rock one more time, finishing with four assists and two points in 13 minutes. It was a departure from Kolek's first three appearances this season, in which he recorded 21 assists and zero turnovers over 44 minutes. The reserve is playing some of his best basketball right now, steadying the offense when Knicks star Jalen Brunson rests. Kolek is taking advantage of an opportunity given to him because of an ankle injury to guard Jose Alvarado . Kolek entered this season on the outside of New York's regular rotation. But his play has been impressive and could make Knicks coach Mike Brown think twice about taking him out of the rotation when Alvarado returns. In Kolek's 57 minutes this season, the Knicks are assisting on 76.5 percent of their baskets, according to NBA Stats, a team high and one that would rank first in the entire league. The club's assist rate drops to 66.3 percent in the minutes he sits. Kolek's careful playmaking comes at a time when the Knicks are in need of good decision making. As of Saturday night, New York ranked 15th in turnovers per 100 possessions. Over the past few years, the Knicks have regularly been one of the better teams at taking care of the ball, ranking 11th in the category last season. The turnover problems have been a factor in New York’s slow offensive start and 2-4 record through the first six games. Kolek has created scoring opportunities for his teammates with ease. Many of Kolek's minutes have been shared with starters Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby . Towns is averaging 5.81 more points per 100 possessions when he shares the floor with Kolek, according to PBP Stats. Anunoby's scoring increases by 9.85 points per 100 possessions in the same scenarios. Since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 NBA Draft, Kolek's role has been inconsistent with New York. Last season, due to a Miles McBride injury, Kolek emerged around the NBA Cup and played a significant role in the Knicks' Cup championship win. He saw regular rotation minutes until the middle of January. The Knicks acquired Alvarado in a trade deadline deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, pushing Kolek further down the depth chart. Crowded backcourt Though it is unclear when Alvarado will return from his injury, he will be back eventually. It creates a competition at the backup point guard slot. With Brunson averaging 35 minutes a night through the last four seasons, there's very limited space to find time for both guards. Add in a small-ish backcourt contributors like McBride, Landry Shamet and Jordan Clarkson , and it seems like a crowded backcourt. Kolek and Alvarado are very different players. Kolek is a floor general with crafty passes and creative finishes around the basket to make up for his lack of athleticism. Alvarado is more of a defensive playmaker, creating havoc with steals. Despite his diminutive stature, Alvarado can situationally guard players larger than him. Both players are inconsistent as three-point shooters but have proven to be capable enough to garner some respect from defenses. It's a good problem to have. The Knicks have relied on the bench to step up in key situations. Last year's run to the championship saw several reserves have individual moments in specific games or series. Brown said in training camp that outside of the starting five, players would be fighting for minutes. Kolek and Alvarado will see some time on the floor this season. Who plays the best will likely earn more time.

stories.title: Winners & Sinners: Week 2
stories.summary: Who and what stood out for the Bucks this week?
stories.detailText: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 26: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks dribbles the ball against Pascal Siakam #43 of the Indiana Pacers in the third quarter at Fiserv Forum on October 26, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Winners & Sinners , where we reflect on the week that was for the Milwaukee Bucks. Week 2 saw the Bucks go 1-2, with the team getting its first win of the season by defeating the arch-rival Indiana Pacers, before being forced into concussion protocols by the Houston Rockets and Cleveland Cavaliers. But who’s deserving of the hardware? MVB Tyler Herro collects his first MVB of the week on the back of efficient shooting in two out of three games and a best-on-court performance against the Pacers: 23 points, 10 rebounds, and seven assists. The shooting was expected, the poise has stood out, and, more importantly, he was Milwaukee’s best when they were at their best, leading the team to its only win of the season thus far. Defensive Belt Defending Champion : Kyle Kuzma. The Contenders: N/A. The Decision: Outside of the win against the Pacers, the Bucks haven’t exactly stopped anyone this week. Myles Turner had some moments in that game, then got mauled by Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley against the Cavaliers, who combined for 52 points on 23/32 shooting (72%) in just 48 minutes. Consider the belt vacated until someone shows enough to earn it. The People’s Champ retired janitor’s wisdom is always appreciated, but this comment—in a quality back-and-forth with naveed2000s—is too good to overlook: Please do go deeper into the early-second-round versus late-first-round draft returns, rj! In the meantime, who’s up for marshmallows? Run That Back This one was simple, or so I thought. Kasparas Jakučionis gets the ball off the swing from Kel’el Ware and thinks like any good point guard does: Return the favour. First, he jabs sideline; buys some space and forces the switch. Then he curls middle, casts the line: one dribble, two dribbles—just enough line to hook Larry Nance, reel him closer. A third follows, a beat to let the water settle. Then it comes, the left- handed spear between rocks. Right to the chest. And before you know it, the catch is in the net. Then, in the week’s waning moments, Brayden Burries does this : INSANE BRAYDEN BURRIES POSTER! 🚨 https://t.co/ftmnY0eBWG — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) November 1, 2026 Gravity -defying stuff—and enough vertical to lift our collective spirits! Sinner(s) Myles Turner : You hate to kick a bloke when he’s down, but Myles Turner has just not been good enough. Not close to it. He was better to start this week against the Pacers, but that game actually proves the point. Turner has been so bad for the Bucks that a six-point, nine-rebound, four-assist, four-block performance, which also came with 29% shooting, three turnovers, and some “efforts” that would lead to a benching for Kel’el Ware, was lauded as a standout night. Following that, he put up just four points and two rebounds against the Rockets before being abused by Allen, Mobley, and whoever else cared to venture into the Bucks’ defensive paint against the Cavaliers. Second Quarters: Against the Pacers, the Bucks hit just 8/24 shots in the second quarter as a two-point quarter-time lead became an 11-point halftime deficit. Against the Rockets, the Bucks hit just 6/24 shots in the second quarter as they let a two-point quarter-time deficit explode to 22 by halftime. Against the Cavaliers, the Bucks hit just 7/28 shots as they let a one-point quarter-time lead transform into a 26-point deficit. This. Is. Not. Going. To. Get. The. Job. Done. For more on the Bucks second-quarter woes, check out their shot charts, courtesy of NBA.com: If… Then… If Nate Ament has already overtaken Ousmane Dieng in the forward rotation, then the 2026 trade-deadline darling has some serious work to do. Dieng’s offseason deal— three years, $17.5m —seemed surprisingly good for the Bucks, but maybe they knew his play down the stretch was more mirage than oasis. That’s all for Week 2. Share your winners and sinners in the comments!

stories.title: Final Five: Breaking down the clutch minutes of the Mavericks’ 116-111 win over the Houston Rockets
stories.summary: The final five minutes of Friday’s 116-111 win was loaded with play worthy of analysis
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 30: Daniel Gafford #21 and Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates during the game against the Houston Rockets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Glenn James/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks (4-2) picked up a huge 116-111 win over the Houston Rockets (5-1) on Friday night in their first NBA Cup game of the season. The road to victory was paved with a slew of clutch plays, with Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving and Daniel Gafford leading the way when it mattered most. The NBA defines the “clutch” as the final five minutes of a game when the score is within five or fewer points. Here we break down that exact scenario from the huge win Friday. 4:21: Tie score, 96-96 The Mavericks entered the clutch with a three-point lead. They forced two stops around a Rockets’ offensive rebound but could not convert on the other end. Again they forced a stop, but yielded another offensive rebound to the Rockets, setting up Fred Van Vleet for a game tying three-point shot. 3:28: Mavs up four, 100-96 Flagg began asserting his clutch-time dominance with an immediate answer to Van Vleet’s three-pointer. At the 4:07 mark, Flagg hit a floater for his 25 th point of the night. After a stop and a rebound, Flagg was at it again with a finger roll that was counted as a score after being goaltended. 2:26 Tie score, 100-100 Zaccharie Risacher committed a shooting foul on the following possessing, giving Kevin Durant a chance to drain two free throws. After an Irving missed three-pointer, Van Vleet connected on a bucket to once again tie the score. 1:40 Mavs up 105-100 With the score tied, it was Irving’s turn to respond. Off a Flagg assist, Irving broke the 30-point threshold with a nice 16-foot shot to put the Mavericks up by two points. Caleb Martin committed a shooting foul on Durant, but the 82.7% free throw shooter missed both attempts. Then it was Flagg’s turn to join Irving as a 30-point scorer as he hit a floater, was fouled and connected on the free throw to extend the lead to five points. COOP AND-1 TO EXTEND THE LEAD 😤 HE'S GOT 30 PTS! MAVS LEAD BY 5 LATE IN Q4. pic.twitter.com/2fhyfDsFYh — NBA (@NBA) October 31, 2026 1:18 Mavs up five, 107-102 Durant hit a shot to quiet the excitement for a moment, but Irving was not deterred. Dribbling up the court, Irving surprising launched a three-point attempt only seven seconds later. The shot was errant, setting up Gafford for an offensive rebound and put-back. Above the rim, his mini hook shot was on a downward trajectory as soon as it left his hand, warranting a goal tending call on Clint Capela to sustain the five-point lead. 1:00 Mavs up two, 107-105 The next sequence of events may find you shining up your tinfoil hat. On a Rockets’ inbounds pass, Durant cut to the rim, then thrust himself backwards onto Caleb Martin who grabbed a handful of Durant’s jersey. The play was reviewed by officials to determine if it was an away-from-the-play foul (a foul committed on court prior to the ball being inbounded, which gives the offended team a free throw and the ball). Replay seemed to clearly show the contact was initiated and followed-through on by Durant, with Martin grabbing him to brace his fall after absorbing contact, but somehow this was not a factor in the review. Instead, Durant hit the free throw and then immediately connected on a jump shot after the inbound. This turn of events could have been foreboding; just a season ago it may have been. The Mavericks were flying high with a five-point lead, but a questionable call made it a one-possession game in a matter of seconds. 0:24 Mavs up four, 109-105 Following the strange away-from-the-ball foul, things got more tenuous. P.J. Washington got sped up, prompting him to pass the ball toward Irving at half court. The pass was off the mark and Amen Thompson collected in stride heading for what would have been a game-tying layup. Irving stepped in for a charge! What again seemed an obvious call, especially due to Thompson’s unquestionable arm extension push-off, was challenged by the Rockets who had nothing to lose in doing so. Improbably, the charge was overturned on the basis Irving did not have legal guarding position prior to Thompson’s slightly lowered shoulder and arm extension. If karma is your thing, the Mavs were beneficiaries of a “ball don’t lie” moment, as Thompson missed both free throws he received by way of the overturned charge. Flagg had enough at this point, extending the game to a two-possession affair with a slick turnaround jumper for a four-point lead. FLAGG SCORES AGAIN IN THE CLUTCH. MAVS UP 3. 7.9 TO PLAY. https://t.co/uHKnPjyaGr pic.twitter.com/3kMsZWaF0U — NBA (@NBA) October 31, 2026 0:11 Mavs up three, 111-108 Following Flagg’s heroics, the Mavs were a stop away from all but ending the game, but Jabari Smith nailed a three from the top of the arc to bring the Rockets within one point. With an obvious free throw shooting contest ready to ensue, the Mavericks got the ball to Gafford who was fouled by Durant for a trip to the foul line. Surely, the Mavs did not want to put Gafford in this position, but the Rockets’ on-ball defense after the Mavs inbounded left them no choice. Gafford was unfazed. He calmly stroked both free throws to give Dallas a three-point lead. 0:06 Mavs up three, 113-110 We learned that Dusty May is inclined to foul the opponent when the Mavs are up by three points with mere second remaining, rather than give the opposition a chance to attempt a three-point shot for the tie. Flagg fouled Durant who hit both free throws to cut the Mavericks’ lead to one point. The Rockets had to return the favor, fouling Irving on the other end. Irving hit both of his free throws to maintain the three-point advantage after the exchange. 0:04 Mavs up three, 114-111 With the three-point advantage, Dallas once again fouled to prevent a Rockets’ three-point attempt. This time, Thompson split his pair, hitting the first and intentionally missing the second. Thompson got the rebound off his own miss, but it was because he entered the lane well before the ball hit the rim, resulting in a lane violation and turnover. On the next possession, the Mavs got a measure of away-from-the-ball revenge. Marcus Smart mauled Flagg before the ball was inbounded, giving Flagg the chance to increase the lead to three points, which he calmly did by hitting his free throw. 0:00 Mavs win 116-111 Irving was fouled once again, giving him a trip to the line. The veteran leader put the game out of reach and ended the free throw shooting train by once again hitting both of his attempts to extend the lead to five, leaving the Rockets with no further options. As he iced the game, Irving was serenaded with chants of “MVP” from the home crowd. MVP CHANTS FOR KYRIE 👏 35 PTS (game-high) 4 REB 9 AST (game-high) 5 3PM (game-high) The Mavs win their opening game in @emirates NBA Cup Group Play! pic.twitter.com/HdiN2rAHa4 — NBA (@NBA) October 31, 2026 In the clutch, Flagg scored 10 points on a perfect 4-of-4 shooting and 2-of-2 from the line. Irving had six points despite missing two three-point attempts. He hit one shot from inside the arc and drained all four of his free throws. This was a dynamic performance by the pair, showing just how poised beyond his years Flagg is and how important Irving is to the success of the team. Flagg was perfect, answering the bell every time with big plays. Irving, while slightly less than perfect, had it where it counted. Giving himself up for what likely should have been a charge and hitting free throws that effectively ended the game demonstrated how lethal the duo can be. Not to be forgotten, Gafford got in on the fun with an offensive rebound off one of Irving’s missed three-pointers and a putback for two points. He then hit two free throws that were absolutely critical in the win. Kyrie: 35 PTS (26 in 2H) 9 AST Coop: 33 PTS (18 in 2H) 6 AST The dynamic duo leads the @dallasmavs to 1-0 in West Group A! pic.twitter.com/6GfHzLBDu7 — NBA (@NBA) October 31, 2026 I invite you to follow me @_80MPH on X, and check back often at Mavs Moneyball for all the latest on the Dallas Mavericks.

stories.title: Boozer And Memphis Grizzlies Move To 6-0
stories.summary: Cameron Boozer is doing Cameron Boozer things again
stories.detailText: PORTLAND, OR - OCTOBER 29: Cameron Boozer #27 of the Memphis Grizzlies handles the ball during the game against the Portland Trail Blazers on October 29, 2026 at the Moda Center in Portland, Oregon. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Cameron Browne/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images O ver at CBS’s Eye on College Basketball podcast, Gary Parrish, who lives in Memphis, has really taken to Grizzlies rookie Cameron Boozer. On the most recent episode, he raved about Boozer being the second-youngest NBA player to record a triple-double, and in just his fifth game, which is remarkable. Using his typical hyperbole, he said that Boozer could come back to college basketball in his spare time and help his team to win there, too. While that’s a bit silly, his sentiment is not far off. In fact, we could start to call it the Boozer Effect. What’s the Boozer Effect? That’s simple: his teams usually win. Memphis, projected to be in a rebuilding year, is instead off to a 6-0 start, and is the only NBA team still undefeated after knocking off Sacramento Saturday night, 136-105. Boozer finished with 27 points, 9 rebounds, and 3 assists (on the downside, he had 7 turnovers). Memphis’s primary rotation players, aside from Boozer, are journeyman Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Jerami Grant, Zach Edey, Cam Spencer, Isaiah Stewart, Scotty Pippen, Jr., GG Jackson, and Quinten Post. Coward is a promising young player, and Edey is massive, but the other guys are basically role players. And now, Jerome and Pippen are both having back issues, while Edey is on a minutes restriction as he continues to work his way back from last season’s injury. Look at it this way: if you took Boozer out of this group, where would they be? It’s impossible to answer, but this seems obvious: they sure as hell wouldn’t be 6-0. stories.title: Rockets defeat Thunder 119-98
stories.summary: Back to the ways of winning!
stories.detailText: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 31: The Houston Rockets huddle up during the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on October 31, 2026 at the Toyota Center in Houston, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Logan Riely/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Houston Rockets rebounded from their first loss of the season Saturday night, crushing the Oklahoma City Thunder 119-98 at the Toyota Center. Jabari Smith Jr. had 30 points and 9 rebounds; Marcus Smart added 24 points. Houston took advantage of one of the Western Conference’s top teams with a strong start, balanced scoring, and great defense for a 21-point victory. Smith shot 10-of-18 from the field, including 6-of-12 on 3-pointers. Smart was 7-of-10 on 3-pointers as the Rockets shot 46% as a team and were 18-of-41 from behind the arc. Jabari Smith Jr. was in his bag tonight in Houston's victory: 🚀 30 PTS (game-high) 🚀 9 REB 🚀 5 AST 🚀 6 3PM The @HoustonRockets are now 6-1! pic.twitter.com/L8xL9n5lkq — NBA (@NBA) November 1, 2026 Alperen Sengun, who returned to the lineup after missing the last two games with lower back soreness, finished with 16 points, 9 rebounds and 10 assists, and Kevin Durant scored 14 points. The victory was a strong comeback for Houston after it lost 116-111 to the Dallas Mavericks on Friday night. The Rockets didn’t let the setback linger as they came out with vigor and took an early lead against Oklahoma City. Oklahoma City couldn’t slow the onslaught since the club was able to share out the scoring burden. Houston also got a boost from its effort on defense, making the Thunder struggle for good shots. The Rockets’ opening quarter set the tone for the rest of the night. Houston led Oklahoma City 35-26 after the first quarter. In the second quarter, the defense really tightened up, holding the defense to just 10 points and carrying a 55-36 lead into the half. Oklahoma City couldn’t find its offensive rhythm in the first half. The Thunder were also without many key players in Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, and Alex Caruso, resulting in a less experienced lineup against Houston. The Thunder tried to adjust, but Houston held on and avoided a late-game meltdown like the one it had in the previous night’s game against Dallas. The Rockets played good offense and did a good job of not letting Oklahoma City get anything going to threaten the advantage. The victory was an especially encouraging one, since Houston made progress in a needed area. The Rockets gave up 40 points in the fourth quarter, squandered an 11-point lead, and struggled on defense against Dallas. Saturday’s performance was a lot better defensive effort and greater control of the game. The win lifts Houston to 6-1 on the season and continues an amazing start that has the team looking like an early contender in the Western Conference. The Rockets hope to carry that energy into their next game against the Boston Celtics on Monday, November 2, in Houston. As always, be sure to check back at The Dream Shake for post- and pre-game coverage.

stories.title: Sandro Mamukelashvili was a fan-fave, but the Raptors need to win this
stories.summary: In the Raptors’ first trip to Los Angeles, Toronto has a chance to stop a cold streak, and prove they can win without Kawhi
stories.detailText: Inglewood, CA - October 28: Forward Sandro Mamukelashvili #54 of the Los Angeles Lakers passes against center Brook Lopez #11 of the LA Clippers in the second half of a NBA basketball game at Intuit Dome in Inglewood on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Raptors’ road trip begins with an LA double feature against the Lakers and the Clippers, starting with the boys in the gold and purple this Sunday, November 1st. This will be Toronto’s first look at either of the Los Angeles teams this season, with both organizations boasting former Raptors under contract — on the Lakers, the beloved Georgian forward Sandro Mamukelashvili, and on the Clippers, former All-Star Brandon Ingram. While Ingram is unfortunately still facing injuries that are keeping him off the court, Mamu will be there to greet his old teammates in full force; this time, looking to topple the red and black. Walking into Crypto.com Arena means not only saying hello to old friendly faces, but staring into the face of some serious adversaries, no one more prominent among them than Luka Dončić. Dončić has won four of his last five contests against the Raptors, and remains a part of a team that has an even more prominent winning streak against Toronto: the Raptors haven’t won against the Lakers since December of 2022, and will be going into this matchup looking to end this longstanding history. In many respects, the Toronto Raptors have matured this year, even beyond the acquisition of Kawhi Leonard. The Raptors are neither a “young” team nor an “old” team at this point. Scottie Barnes is 25 years old, RJ Barrett is 26, and Immanuel Quickley is 27. But beyond age, the Raps are playing with a maturity unlike anything they’ve displayed in previous years, most prominently among them Scottie Barnes. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Mark Blinch/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Still early in the season, Barnes has demonstrated that his offensive game has developed exponentially over the offseason, and since the 2026 playoffs, he has looked able to shoulder a massive two-way load, defending, facilitating, and creating his own looks. His midrange game has looked to be on-par with the greats this season, something all the more important when facing off against a team with a premiere centre. With Kawhi Leonard still out, Scottie and his teammates have stepped up to fill the void left by his phantom scoring and clamping defence, and will need every bit of paint-pounding bucket-getting and hard nosed D against the Lakers. With a record of 4-2 on the season, the Lakers are off a three game winning streak and are equipped with weapons the Toronto Raptors will be hard-pressed to manage. Walker Kessler at 7’2” is a nightmare matchup for the Raptors, clogging the paint for RJ and Scottie, that Jakob Poeltl will need to step up in a big way for on the defensive end. Kessler can score and rebound, but is swatting shots at a disgusting rate, with 17 blocks in five games, including a 9 stock performance that made the Lakers look like they got more than their money’s worth for the big man. How Walker Kessler is anchoring the Lakers defense https://t.co/9d6OFGuNGr — Silver Screen and Roll (@LakersSBN) October 28, 2026 Poeltl, who had a double double in a comeback game against Orlando, will likely split minutes at centre with Collin Murray-Boyles and Trayce Jackson-Davis, but as the Raptors’ starter, getting in the paint and banging with the other team’s seven-footer is going to be his primary responsibility. Yak has a chance tonight to continue his path back to the up-and-up, and the success of tonight’s game will rest in large part on his shoulders. Containing Luka Magic and Austin Reaves is no easy feat either, but one which the Raptors are moderately more equipped to do. Scottie will likely take the Dončić assignment himself, as he matches up with with the big man’s stature and abilities the best, but to see how Ja’Kobe Walter handles Austin Reaves will be of interest as well, with the young guard suddenly thrust into the starting lineup. Throughout the season, Barnes and Barrett have both shown that they’re capable of taking over offensively when necessary, and tonight will be a game where they will likely have to do just that. Surviving these rough matchups without Kawhi is the name of the game when making him a big part of the team, and tonight will be a chance for the Raptors to further distance themselves from the collapse in Minnesota against another top-5 guard in the league.

stories.title: Inside the Suns: Lineup changes, defense, and center options
stories.summary: Your weekly Inside the Suns analysis straight from the BSotS community who live and breathe the team.
stories.detailText: Welcome to Inside the Suns, a deep-dive analysis of the current Phoenix Suns team in which the Fantable — a roundtable of Bright Siders — give their takes on the Suns’ latest issues and news. Fantable Questions of the Week Q1: How long are you willing to wait (in terms of games played) to give the Suns’ starting unit time to (hopefully) gel before pronouncing it DOA and demanding changes? zenzino: The wording of this question cracks me up. ‘Demanding changes’. Like we have any actual say in what happens. Blow it up now! Just kidding. So much impatience. The NBA season is a marathon, not a sprint. And the starting gun just went off. What’s worse than the Suns’ play is the Suns’ schedule. 11 days into the season, and the Suns have played 3 games. Leaves us lots of time in between to contemplate the sky falling. I’d give it 15-20 games if there were some kind of progress along the way. All this talk about continuity seems to make us forget that the starters have a distinct lack thereof. 2 of the 5 are new to the lineup, and even the returning 3 starters of Book, Brooks, and Green had only played 10 games together before this season. This should be considered a brand new starting lineup. While the starting 5 have not yet gelled, I think there are bigger issues throughout the lineup. As Tom wrote earlier this week, the Suns’ culture and ‘alignment’ are in question. As Keratosis pointed out in the comments, everyone is talking about trading Green, and he’s the only one who has been consistent on both ends of the court. Of course, the players need to act like highly paid professionals. However, as I’ve maintained since the KD days, the leadership has to start at the top with the head coach. This is a huge test of Ott and probably BG because he’s so involved. The culture and standards have to be consistently maintained and nurtured, not just given lip service. You don’t just get to pick up where you left off last season… or maybe you do, and that’s what the Suns are doing. Ashton: Rod is setting this whole series of questions up as a chance to throw shade at the Suns. I am going to take the high road and throw shade at the Suns. Good question? Coach Ott has now had four days to try to get his team on the same page between games. I really hope film review with the players was part of it. Coach Ott says it was a communication issue between him and the players. I am not so sure. It seems like a chemistry issue or at the very least a preparation issue. I am just not optimistic about the Suns turning this around anytime soon, but I guess I am willing to give them four weeks to show improvement and two months before pronouncing them “DOA”. There are not many changes to demand as the starting four is basically set, but I am willing to climb on board with CG possibly starting as Green still seems to seek the ISO plays. If Booker goes off for another three points, I may seriously consider bringing in Goody’s defense in place of Booker minutes. Rod: I’m close now, but the absences of both Mark Williams and Oso Ighodaro and the total reliance on Khaman Maluach as the starting center makes me believe that I shouldn’t be too hasty. Duop Reath as the primary backup hasn’t worked out well either, but I also can’t reasonably blame all of the starters’ problems on this. At this point, I’m kind of in a holding pattern until Oso gets healthy and we can get a look at how well things work out before giving the starting lineup the last rites. I don’t expect a miracle turnaround, but if I don’t see some evidence of better play after 10 games (following his return), then I’ll be fully on board with trying just about anything that has a chance of improving. Starting Gillespie and moving Green to a 5th man bench role is the obvious 1st move to try. After that, I’m game with just about any other lineup experiment that has any kind of a shot at improving things. Q2: Three games into the season and the Suns have THE worst-ranked defense in the NBA. What are your thoughts on why they’ve been so bad on D? zenzino: It would be easy to blame it on the addition of Bridges and the absence of Williams and Oso. Maluach was supposed to have time to ease into the main rotation, and now he’s been thrust into the starting lineup. On the aforementioned fact that even the returning starters haven’t had much time playing together before this season. Those are factors to be sure, but something else just isn’t right. It’s not just the starters. While the 2nd is better than the starting unit, they still aren’t what we are used to from them. As the ‘look on the bright side’ guy in this, I still have to wonder whether the first half of last season was an anomaly and the post-All-Star-break version is who they actually are. I might conclude that Mark Williams is the most underrated Suns player. He wasn’t fancy or flashy, but he got the job done in a myriad of ways and was a defensive anchor for this team. All that talk on media day about how they worked all summer together and are chomping at the bit to get the season started… I got excited. And now it rings hollow. All that being said, it’s only been 3 games. Anyone who throws in the towel after 3 tries at anything will never win. Again, from my perspective, this needs to get fixed from the coaching side. The players also need to hold each other accountable, but that starts with the coach. Ashton: It appears that Miles Bridges is missing multiple assignments and may make the list for worst trade of the year. Booker is visibly frustrated at the defense (and his own shooting). And teams know that the “Center can not hold”. That is a shoutout to poet William Butler Yeats, and as dark as it is, it remains one of my favorite poems. It easily sums up the early Suns games, as I am not sure if there is a “Second Coming”. However, Oso was upgraded to questionable for Friday’s game against Denver. This comes back to team unity on both sides of the floor, and that is lacking. Suns were universally expected to suck last season and took defense to a chip-on-the-shoulder level. I would have liked to be able to evaluate the Denver Nuggets’ game Friday night, which Jokic has already called “their defense sucks,” but let’s see which team wins that award. Still, the Suns being last in so many defensive metrics in three games is beyond concerning; it is condemning. Rod: I honestly believe it’s a combination of things, roster additions/subtractions and injuries being the top 2. I mostly see the effort on the court, but one blown assignment, one offensive rebound given up because you’re out of position, one missed switch can undo all the effort put in. Having two of your top rotation players at the same position (Williams and Ighodaro) has got to hurt both units, especially when your 4th guy in line at that position (Reath) has never been considered even a fair defensive player. Looking at the numbers, the starting unit has actually been the worst defensively (29th), while the bench has been at least marginally better (20th), though not enough to make a big difference. We’re just three games into the season, though, and hopefully things will improve as the team gets more accustomed to the new additions (Bridges & Kennard), Oso returns to stabilize the rotation, and perhaps some lineup changes are made that give the starting lineup some more defensive muscle. Q3: With Oso Ighodaro out for the GSW and OKC games, Jordan Ott has mostly played “small ball” lineups when Khaman Maluach is on the bench, with backup center Doup Reath averaging only 5 minutes per game in those two outings. If Oso is going to miss much more time, what backup center options (other than Reath) should the Suns consider? zenzino: Unlike most people here, the term ‘small ball’ doesn’t make me angry or fill my heart with dread. It is a viable strategy that I’ve watched win championships. The Suns just need to get better at it, and you can only get better at something with practice. Bring it on! It really depends on how ‘much more’ time we are talking about. If we’re talking a week or two, I don’t think the Suns should strain themselves to find another backup. A month or two? Maybe something needs to be done. However, we haven’t seen Timme yet. He’s a lighter version of Oso, so maybe they can get by with center by committee. I believe someone more familiar with college basketball than I am said that Sheer used to play small-ball 5 in college. If so, add him to the committee. I just don’t know that there’s anyone out there for the vet min who could make a difference compared to what we have now. Everyone mentions Olynyk, but he’s playing in Europe now. I wouldn’t hate Bismack Part II, but I don’t think that would move the needle. Addendum: Oso has been practicing with the team. Ott says that it just depends on how Oso’s body responds to the workouts. So, we’re probably talking days and not weeks. Oso haters, skip this part. Everyone else, we’re going to see a big difference in this team with Oso. He is the connector. On defense and offense. Adding a passer and playmaker can only help the offense starving for it. While not a rim protector, his on-ball and team defense are key. Everything will work better with him on the court. Ashton: It is political season. There is more lying than ever, and only sports can match it when it comes to injury reports. I think Oso will be out for more than two games, but that statement may not age well. Also, my favorite day in November is not the fourth but the fifth. That is when all the unwanted ads, calls, and texts shut the hell up. The cupboard is bare when it comes to backup center options. So, Ott is forced into small-ball for what could be a while. The only answer I have to this is to maybe roll the dice on Koa Peat and see what Drew Timme (who is also out) can do as a little bigger unit off the bench without a center. I really have no idea why Doup Reath is averaging five minutes per game. I thought that stat was startling. He needs more minutes. Rod: First off, I believe that looking at signing a free agent center to fill that open 15th roster spot is not something the Suns should try…at least not yet. Anyone who is still a free agent at this time of the year, well, there’s usually a very good reason why, and not a good one. If Oso was definitely going to be out for a long stretch of the season, then I’d give it some serious thought, but only then. At this point, Oso is going to be back on the court before a new guy has had enough time to learn the Suns’ offensive and defensive schemes to be more than an obstacle to cohesive team play, let alone a positive addition. Frankly, I think that’s why Timme actually hasn’t been active yet. He wasn’t around for training camp or any of the preseason games and needs some time to actually learn how things work before being thrown into the fray. Some have suggested giving Fleming a try, but the guy’s still not playing instinctively at PF, so I doubt he’d really be very effective playing out of position at center. Playing small ball with Bridges at the 5 spot isn’t the answer, but at least he’s a big body with several years of NBA-level experience who won’t react like a deer in headlights when thrust into a changed role. All things considered, I’m fine with rolling with things as they are for now, with Reath getting at least a few minutes a game to see if he’s not having a good night before going small. Hopefully, Oso will be back very soon, and we won’t have to have this conversation again… for a while, at least. As always, many thanks to our Fantable members for all their extra effort this week! Quotes of the Week “It’s early. Can’t expect to be perfect right now.” – Jordan Goodwin “We need to play faster. I think we have an opportunity when we do that. If we get stops, we get rebounds, we’re able to push the pace offensively and just create a lot of different things on the offensive end.” _ Luke Kennard “Overall, we have to stick with some of things that we’ve talking about all camp because we did see success before the regular season started. We’ve got to give this a little bit of grace of couple more games just in general, both sides of ball. I think we have higher standards for what we want to do.” – Jordan Ott “We’re just figuring each other out. It’s third game of the season. We’ve been figuring each other out. Once we do, I think we’re going to be a really good team.” – Miles Bridges Suns Trivia/History Book closes his 20s with the 11th-most career points in @NBA history by a player before turning 30 📚 The list of players he's in company with: LeBron James, Kobe Bryant, Wilt Chamberlain, Kevin Durant, Michael Jordan, Carmelo Anthony, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Oscar Robertson,… pic.twitter.com/HKhOOZHr6t — Phoenix Suns (@Suns) October 30, 2026 On November 1, 1996, 8-time All-Star Steve Nash made his NBA debut for the Phoenix Suns in a 96-82 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers. In his first game, Nash racked up zeros in points, assists, rebounds, steals, etc. in 5 minutes of court time. It was not until his 2nd game on the following night (Nov. 2) that Nash recorded the first assist and the first basket of his Hall of Fame career in a 110-95 loss to the Houston Rockets. Nash’s totals in that game were 9 points, 1 assist, 1 rebound, and 1 steal in 12 minutes. Although Steve played the fewest minutes of any Sun in this game, he led the team in trips to the free-throw line and shot 6-for-7 for the night. On November 2, 1999, 4-time All-Star Shawn Marion made his NBA debut for the Phoenix Suns in a 107-102 loss to the Denver Nuggets. Marion recorded his first NBA double-double in the game with 14 points and 14 rebounds. He would get 6 more double-doubles during the rest of his rookie season plus 1 more in the first round of the playoffs. On November 2, 1990, the Suns defeated the Utah Jazz 119-96 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium in Japan, in the first regular-season game played outside North America by any major professional sports league. Tom Chambers led the Suns with 38 points and 10 rebounds while Kevin Johnson scored 29 with 10 assists. 1-time All-Star Cedric Ceballos made his NBA debut in this game, scoring 2 points and grabbing 1 rebound in just 2 minutes of court time. On November 7, 1992, the Suns celebrated their 30th Anniversary season by moving into the America West Arena where they opened their season with a 111-105 win over the LA Clippers. Charles Barkley (acquired by trade after the end of the previous season) wowed the Phoenix home crowd with a near triple-double (37 points, 21 rebounds and 8 assists) in his first regular season game as a Sun.
