stories.title: The Dallas Mavericks are fun again
stories.summary: Wins over Indiana, Miami and Houston have turned the tables on expectations for the Mavericks entering the season.
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 30: Zaccharie Risacher #10 of the Dallas Mavericks grabs the rebound during the game against the Houston Rockets during the Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Garrett Ellwood/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images When the clock struck triple zeroes on Friday night, I could only lean back on my couch and smile. The Dallas Mavericks (4-2) had defeated the previously undefeated Houston Rockets; Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving combined for 68 points. It continued a three-game winning streak in which the Mavericks vanquished three playoff contenders, and their second game in a row knocking-off an undefeated team. The game had massive swings in emotion and momentum . The atmosphere in the American-Airlines center hasn’t reached that level since the 2024 playoffs. The Mavericks, after a year-and-a-half of absolute misery (save for winning the lottery), are seemingly back to bringing fans joy. This team is really, really, fun. They play fast and aggressive on both ends, often passing up a good shot to create a great one. They may not have elite personnel on either end, but the players know their roles, and they play to their strengths. Instead of playing a static defense that relies on individual efforts from great defenders, they relentlessly swarm and scram ball-handlers into making mistakes, using their absurdly lengthy wings to disrupt opponet ryhthym. On offense they simply attack the rim no matter what, using this constant rim pressure to set up open looks from long range. All of this starts with a 19-year-old superstar who simply doesn’t understand that 19-year-olds are supposed to be in college, not dominating the best league in the world. But it isn’t just Cooper Flagg’s play. It’s his relentless, unyielding energy on both sides that feeds the rest of the team. He’s constantly attacking the basket with the force of a runaway mustang, using this gravity to get his teammates involved. But it isn’t just force, it’s the unexplainable floater touch that appeared out of thin-air last season. Put simply, Flagg refuses to let this team lose, and he will be dammed if they repeat last season’s catastrophic play. But unlike last season, he isn’t alone; a New Jersey basketball wizard has his back. Kyrie Irving was relatively quiet until Friday night’s showcase, which is understandable given the near 19-month layoff after ACL reconstruction, but he was anything but quiet in the second half against the Rockets. Irving scored 26 points in the final two quarters on only 13 shots. This included multiple patented Kyrie Irving transition pull-up 3-pointers that set the arena into a frenzy. His ability to feel the ebbs and flows within a game is special; knowing when to attack and when to let someone else take the reins. The Mavericks made their fourth-quarter run without Flagg on the court, and much of that is due to Irving’s mastery. But let’s not forget the other number one overall pick on the roster. Zaccahrie Risacher exemplifies what makes this team special. He was cast aside by the Hawks. Written off by most of the basketball world, including me. Instead of letting the dire circumstances torpedo his career, he’s embraced what is necessary to succeed in the NBA. He is ruthless on defense, constantly attacking the basketball to the tune of almost 4 combined steals and blocks per game this season. His offense is far from perfect, but there hasn’t been a Maverick wing who attacks the glass like he does in a long time. Before the season there was only one thing that I wanted to see from the Mavericks team, watchable basketball. It’s truly hard to put into words how terrible they were to watch last season. It was a constant swirl of frustration, anger, spite and stubbornness. Now? Not only are the Mavericks are must-see TV, they’re also pretty damn good.

stories.title: Stumbling gracefully through my first game with a Celtics credential
stories.summary: My first night covering the Celtics as credentialed media, from getting lost in hallways to going 0-for-4 on questions.
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MA - OCTOBER 30: Paul George #13 of the Boston Celtics celebrates during the game against the Chicago Bulls during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Babineau/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images I’ve been a Celtics fan most of my life. For the first time, I had to be something a bit more than that. On Friday, October 30th, I had the incredible honor of making my debut as a credentialed media member for CelticsBlog when the Celtics faced the Bulls in the NBA Cup. Growing up in Massachusetts, I’ve been all about Boston sports since I was a kid. Me at 13 for my first Celtics Game My love for basketball and the Celtics intensified as I got older, and I’ve spent the last 10 years studying the game hard, finding a relationship between improving my own skills on the court and understanding the intricacies of NBA hoops. At some point along the way I had more opinions, and needed room to share them without bugging everyone in my life. I took to Twitter, finding community among like-minded fans who loved the game and a good argument. Over time, that sharpened my ability to understand what I was seeing and articulate it to others. Flash forward to now, this voice I’ve found — boosted by several seasons writing for CelticsBlog — has allowed me to fulfill a dream, and it was honestly surreal. From receiving the notice that my credential request was accepted on Tuesday, to driving into Boston on Friday, I felt a sense of jitters that have only really been exceeded by my wedding day. It wasn’t nerves based around fears, rather it was about passion and the fulfillment of something that I care deeply about. I wanted to do a good job, and make the most of this opportunity. From the moment I walked up to the arena, I had to embrace the uncertainty. I immediately asked for guidance from a parking attendant on where I could find the media entrance. Once I made my way inside, I asked for more directions and was pointed toward the desk to pick up my credentials. I clumsily walked through the metal detector with my backpack on, laughing at myself for the mistake — one I had just read that my colleague Grant Burfiend made as well. With Grant’s other cautionary tale in mind, I made sure to ask for the appropriate floor in the elevator. Once I reached my destination, I tentatively followed the labyrinth of hallways until I found the media dining room. I plopped my bag down at a table, poured up a hot coffee and tried to take stock of where things were at, looking around occasionally to see if there were any familiar faces. I downed the coffee and decided it was probably time to find the press conference room for the pregame availability. I’d like to preface this by saying that I generally think my navigation skills are pretty solid, but I needed the assistance of about three people to get me through the maze of hallways and toward the conference room. My welcome to the NBA moment came during this time when a large voice offered a polite “Excuse me”. I moved to the side, now a little less confident about where I was going, and watched as the colossal Mitchell Robinson strolled past me. Eventually, I ended up in what clearly looked to be the press conference room. Though as I took my seat and waited for several minutes as the only person seated in there, I questioned if I was in the right place. Fortunately my initial instincts were correct, and people started filing in over the next 10 minutes or so. Where is everyone There were a ton of people I recognized, but didn’t quite have the right level of ease to start introducing myself before the availability kicked off. I listened as Tony Dobbins filled in for Joe Mazzulla, answering questions about their big man group, and Mitchell Robinson’s performance so far. Once the questions concluded, I followed the herd out of the room and found a moment to introduce myself to Noa Dalzell and Jack Simone. They both offered a bit of insight, and led the way to the room for the visiting team’s availability. While waiting for Tiago Splitter to enter, I said hello to the wonderful Sam LaFrance. Sam gave me some more valuable info, including the important fact that dinner would be $10, cash only. With no cash in my wallet, he graciously offered to cover it for me and would not accept my Venmo offer later on. That was a great gesture, and one I hope to pay back at a game in the future. Meeting those three helped me feel more relaxed, and I shared my dinner with another introduction to the great First to the Floor trio of Ben Vallis, Jake Issenberg, and Wayne Spooney. I spoke with them for a while, along with CelticsBlog’s Gio Rivera, who I relied on for more guidance on getting from the dining room to the court for warmups. I spent time taking it in court side and chatting more with the First to the Floor lads. As we watched different players get warmed up, a chaperone with the Boston Children’s Hospital spotted our press passes and commented that being this close must feel regular for us. Not quite. With it being my first game with a pass and the freedom to roam the perimeter of the court, I mentioned that it felt just as exciting for me. With about 40 minutes before tip, we made our way up to the press seats, again navigating through curtained entrances and unclear corridors. Once in my assigned seat, I took another moment to appreciate the gravity of the evening. This was something I’ve thought about for a long time, and my goal was to just be present and enjoy. My view from press row before tip-off against the Bulls. As the game got underway I locked into analysis mode. The press seats are in the highest perch of the arena, but several of us agreed that the vantage point is actually great for seeing everything unfold during a possession. In press row, my lens had to change. There’s no cheering, just observation and objectivity. I found accepting that really helped me focus on the finer points of the game, and analyze the trends worth writing a game piece about. Occasionally I could feel my inner fan rising. It’s hard to watch Payton Pritchard drain a three after making Norman Powell stumble without having some type of reaction. I spotted a lot of aggressive defensive coverages that resulted in deflections and turnovers — a trend that I’ve been tracking since preseason. As the game carried on I settled on that being the direction I wanted to take, with the hope that I could get a question or two answered in post-game availability. After the final buzzer, the group in the balcony trekked down the stairs after the freight elevator refused to arrive. We made it down three floors, and walked into the great migration of fans leaving through the main stairwell. We accompanied that group for a few flights before exiting into the loge level. From there we walked down through the court and into the tunnel. We made it back to the press conference room and took our seats to wait for Mazzulla. I spun my question around in my head for a while, trying to land on the right words that could garner some level of interest from Mazzulla. Before I found the right combination, all questions had been asked, and the coach was on his way out the door. I missed the window, but fortunately there were responses that hit the right notes for me to work with. After a few minutes Pritchard stepped into the room. He was introspective about meeting the standards Mazzulla holds him to, highlighting his defense as a point of emphasis against the Bulls. Payton Pritchard’s postgame availability I was still getting a feel for the etiquette of question asking. From my perspective, it was a discreet and well practiced dance of eye contact, head nods and half-raised hands to make it known that you’d like the microphone. I hadn’t found the rhythm of that yet and went 0/4 on the night for chances to ask a question. While slightly disappointing, it’s hard to feel that bad about it. I was basically an undrafted rookie in a room of established vets. The answers given were enough, and I was able to complete my piece on their defensive impact in good time. I walked 12 minutes to the parking garage, reflecting on the evening as I passed endless streams of costumed Bostonians celebrating Halloweekend. I felt grateful to CelticsBlog for helping to facilitate this, and a reassuring sense of confidence that with a lot of the unknowns now understood, I could come back in the future focusing on the most important parts of the job. It was great to meet and watch many of the journalists I respect, and to get to know them a bit. It’s given me a greater appreciation for the machine that is game day coverage. Hopefully with enough reps I’ll manage to learn the secrets of securing a microphone and can break my current streak of unasked questions. For now, I’m glad to have stumbled my way through an unforgettable evening with occasional spurts of grace.

stories.title: Gui Santos' encore to breakout for Warriors hinges on a simple characteristic
stories.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Gui Santos made two easy decisions in 2026, and he carried that mindset into his preparation for the 2026-27 season.
stories.detailText: Gui Santos' encore to breakout for Warriors hinges on a simple characteristic originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area SAN FRANCISCO – Signing a three-year, $15 million contract at the end of February last season was monumental in Gui Santos ’ journey. Life-changing money represented a road from Brazil to the second round of the 2022 NBA Draft as the No. 55 overall pick, years of developing in the G League and now becoming one of basketball’s best stories as one of the Warriors’ key players. Inking the contract was a no-brainer for Santos, though it quickly looked like a steal for the Warriors. Santos will always believe signing instead of hitting restricted free agency was an easy decision. A little more than four months later, Santos is even more sure he made the best decision of his life by marrying his longtime girlfriend Julia Lawrenz last July in her hometown of Curitiba, Brazil. “Julia, she’s a real partner,” Santos said after Warriors open practice, days before the start of the regular season. “She really understands me really well. There’s days where you don’t want to do nothing, you just want to chill, she’s there with me. But there’s days where for some reason you have a bad practice or bad game, she’s the one that helps me leave that behind and think about the next game or next practice. “It’s been really good, she’s been helping me a lot.” Santos has never second-guessed his forever commitment to Julia, and the Warriors feel they’ve struck gold in their commitment to him. He was one of the breakout NBA players last season. The key to his encore isn’t so much about a single skill like shooting. Santos’ next steps center around what he has been best at the past few months off the court: Decision-making. Santos was inactive for the game last season when Jimmy Butler tore his ACL against the Miami Heat on Jan.19. The Warriors’ season came to a halt when Butler held his knee on the Chase Center floor. They had to move on as quickly as they could, and Santos soon found himself in a much different role. Instead of being mainly an energizer, Santos was relied upon much more as a scorer with the ball in his hands. Santos averaged 14.3 points per game the rest of the regular season, starting 28 of the 35 games he played, and shot over 50 percent from the field. But Santos also averaged 2.2 turnovers per game in the span, including nine games of at least four turnovers. He averaged just 0.8 turnovers per game in his first 33 games of the season, starting just twice and scoring only 3.7 points per game. “I’ve talked to him about this,” Warriors coach Steve Kerr said at practice, the day before the final preseason game. “I thought late last season was great for him to have to take on that playmaking responsibility without Jimmy, without Steph. He made a lot of mistakes, but he made a lot of great plays. So this year is more about improving the assist-to-turnover ratio. Make the plays that you have to make, but be more cautious. You don’t need to be wild.” With a healthy Steph Curry scoring a combined 75 points in the Warriors’ last two games, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg having the ability to score 20 and even 30 points, and Brandin Podziemski continuing to progress as a scorer, Santos now can complement them while sliding into a role that better serves his style. “Last year you had to be a little wild at times to try to force things because we didn’t have enough. We have enough now,” Kerr says, regarding his message to Santos. “… We can’t force the issue, and I think sometimes he is forcing the issue, but he’s perfectly cut out to play the style we’re playing, because he’s got a lot of skill.” Kerr’s message came after a preseason game in which Santos had three turnovers, and five the previous game. He didn’t commit any in the preseason finale after Kerr’s talking points. Though the Warriors didn’t yet know what they had in Lendeborg, they knew Santos’ being free with the ball needed to be reigned in. That was the message relayed to him going into the offseason, and it translated into how he took on his training. Santos has considerably changed his body from when he weighed less than 200 pounds before being drafted to now being a strong 225 pounds on his 6-foot-7 frame. His 3-point shot is now part of his arsenal, and his footwork around the rim can be ranked among basketball’s best. Each drill training in Brazil centered around what to do next, what decision was best for himself and the team. “First thing was my decision-making,” Santos says of his offseason focus. “Every time I was doing some drill, the goal of the drill was to make sure I get into the paint and have control of the game. I need to know where I’m going to pass the ball next, how I’m going to go up, how I’m going to use my step-through and footwork to get around guys so I can finish. That was the thing I worked on most during the offseason.” When asked how he felt about his game going into the season, Santos’ answer was hardly about himself. It was a reflection of still being the player who provides energy, and now refining the little things that lead to wins. “I’ve got to take care of the ball and help on the defensive end,” Santos said. “We need to keep Steph 100 percent on offense, so I will be the one to run always on defense. I’m the guy who will do whatever they need me to do.” Santos, however, isn’t feeling 100 percent healthy. He’s closer to 85 percent as he deals with left knee tendinitis, but told NBC Sports Bay Area that he’d much rather play at less than full strength and give his team everything he has than have them be more hampered as a short-handed team. That’s his decision to make, and the Warriors’ medical staff clearing him. Golden State is hungry for wins after turning around a 0-3 start, and Santos is an essential puzzle piece. The key to his encore season after his breakout isn’t about massive leaps. It’s about him honing in on who he had to become last season through smart decisions this season, and continuing to represent a Portuguese phrase he prides himself on: vontade de vencer . Santos translates the words as “a desire to win.” Download and follow the Dubs Talk Podcast

stories.title: Kings players must help ‘special' rookie Darius Acuff Jr., Doug Christie states
stories.summary: No. 7 overall draft pick Darius Acuff Jr. is leading all NBA rookies with 26.3 per game, but the Sacramento Kings remain winless this season.
stories.detailText: Kings players must help ‘special' rookie Darius Acuff Jr., Doug Christie states originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. is exceeding the hype that followed him after Sacramento made him the 2026 No. 7 overall pick. Two weeks into the 2026-27 NBA season, Acuff leads all rookies, averaging 26.3 points per game. The Chicago Bulls’ No. 4 overall pick, Caleb Wilson, is second at 21.2. But while Acuff looks like a budding superstar, the Kings are 0-6 after a 136-105 drubbing at the hands of the 6-0 Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night at FedExForum. Kings coach Doug Christie didn’t waste any time after Saturday’s loss identifying what needs to change. “Man, we have to help him,” Christie told reporters in Memphis. “It’s an absolute must. The kid is special. He’s highly competitive. He wants to win. I truly enjoyed coaching him and watching his growth already in just these games. I think the opponent, a lot of times, tells you what they think about your players and last time we faced these guys, I think they put seven people on him. “So in his third game, that’s telling you who they think he is and that’s what we already know, management, obviously, and myself, is, he’s special, continues to develop, continues to compete. We put him in position to win ball games and he’s going to win a lot of them.” Acuff scored a career-high 38 points in Saturday’s loss, two days after scoring a then-career-high 34 points in the Kings’ 12-point loss to the New Orleans Pelicans. He has scored at least 33 points in three of his six NBA games. Against the Grizzlies, only three other Kings players scored in double figures: De’Andre Hunter had 19 points, while veterans Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis finished with 11 apiece. Sacramento’s bench, led by veteran guard Malik Monk, scored 20 total points in Memphis and is averaging an NBA-worst 19.5 points per game. On defense, the Kings are giving up 128.3 points per game, second-worst in the NBA behind the Bulls, who are allowing 129.3 points per game. But Sacramento is scoring just 109.3 points per game, leading to an NBA-worst 19.0-point differential. So, while Acuff’s stats are eye-popping, the soon-to-be 20-year-old is focused on the Kings’ defense . “Yeah, it’s good to have a flow going but we got to hang our hat on the defensive end, just try to come up with more stops, we’ve got to keep communicating and just try to stay together,” Acuff told reporters when asked about his performances so far as a rookie. Pushed to talk about making an NBA-rookie record-tying nine 3-pointers against the Grizzlies, Acuff still wasn’t in the mood to talk about himself. “It’s good, personal-wise, but it don’t matter because we’re losing, so them two don’t go well together. So it doesn’t really matter,” Acuff said. Christie and Acuff know the rest of the Kings’ roster needs to step up. Maybe injured players like Maxime Raynaud, Keegan Murray and Dylan Cardwell will help when they return. But until they do, Sacramento needs more from LaVine, Sabonis, Hunter and Monk. Otherwise, Acuff might be on an island for a while. Download and follow The Deuce & Mo Podcast

stories.title: Austin Reaves took the blame for the struggles of the second unit vs. Warriors
stories.summary: The Lakers struggled without Luka Dončić on the floor against the Warriors and Austin Reaves took the blame for that.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 30: Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after the Lakers made a basket against the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Austin Reaves is never one to duck the blame or shift the focus to something else. When he’s bad, he’ll admit he’s bad . And on Friday, he was bad. Reaves turned the ball over eight times , shot 9-19 from the field and had a plus-minus of -13, worst among the starters. He was not the sole reason the team blew a 25-point first half lead to the Warriors and lost by double digits , but when you get the superstar contract, you also get the superstar treatment in losses. Debating just how much blame he deserved is irrelevant as Reaves was as brutally honest about his game as anyone else would have been. “I was terrible again. That’s it.” Harsh, but fair. When Luka Dončić was on the floor, the Lakers were great, though mostly because of him. When he sat, the Lakers were bad, with Reaves at the center of it. If you were looking for an excuse, the fact that those non-Luka groups consist of many players who joined the team this offseason is a fair one. Those units are looking for chemistry, but when asked if that’s legitimate rationale for their struggles, Austin wasn’t interested in any excuses. “It’s real, but that doesn’t give that second unit an excuse to be pretty terrible,” he said. “And that starts with me. I’ll watch the film and try to be better. But you have to learn on the fly and pick up things quickly. As I said, I have to be better to start that.” Austin has modeled his career around constant improvement, so there’s little doubt this is just another hurdle he’ll have to climb. Even if he’s run second units without Luka before, they’ve often come flanked by LeBron James. This is a new challenge and teams have him one rung higher on the scouting report now. The word is out that the way to disrupt Austin is to throw doubles at him on ball screens and try to overwhelm him physically into a turnover. That’s the punch defenses are throwing and now it’s time for Austin to throw a counterpunch. Hopefully that one isn’t terrible. stories.title: Lakers vs. Raptors Preview: Bounce back game
stories.summary: The Lakers look to get back on the winning column against the Raptors on Sunday.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 18: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket against Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors during the first quarter at Crypto.com Arena on January 18, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Toronto Raptors 110-93. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Lakers (4-2) have another back-to-back with the Toronto Raptors (3-2) on Sunday. The purple and gold will be at home for these next two games. Start time and TV schedule Who: Los Angeles Lakers vs. Toronto Raptors When: 6 p.m. PT, Nov. 1 Where : Crypto.com Arena Watch: Spectrum Sportsnet The Lakers’ loss to the Golden State Warriors on Friday will certainly be in the running for one of their worst defeats this season. When it comes to games like this, the best thing to do is take note of what went wrong and delete the tape, especially after that first quarter. Three things went wrong for the purple and gold in that game. For starters, they struggled mightily whenever Luka Dončić was on the bench. Second, they committed a season-high 20 turnovers, with Austin Reaves accounting for eight. Lastly, the Warriors simply played harder and smarter than the Lakers. So now, how does Los Angeles respond to their worst loss of the young season thus far? We’ll know when they take on a very good Raptors team on Sunday. The Raptors enter this game having the third-best defense in the league. They won’t have Kawhi Leonard , but they have capable scorers like Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley. They may look like the same Raptors team the Lakers have faced over the years, but make no mistake, this group has developed and is better than ever. As a defensive-first team, these Raptors ranked second in steals and are an above-average transition team, so the Lakers really have to take care of the ball in this one. Toronto will also attempt to expose the Lakers’ weakness in rebounding, knowing they now rank dead last in the league in rebounds per game. The Lakers can’t be outworked once again if they want to win this game. LA has to force the Raptors to execute in the half court, where their offense is less reliable. It would be nice to see a better performance from Reaves and Walker Kessler who has been quite mediocre for his standards over the last couple of games. Reaves and Dončić will face a lot of ball pressure and physicality, so they’ll have to counter with their ability to manipulate the defense and control the game’s pace. After suffering their first loss of the season against the Portland Trail Blazers, the Lakers wasted no time responding, coming out firing and cruising past the L.A. Clippers the following day. Now, the Lakers have another opportunity to bounce back from their worst loss of the young season. It’ll be interesting to see how they respond and what adjustments they make moving forward. Let’s see if they can execute better and more importantly, get back on the winning column against the Raptors on Sunday. Notes and Updates For the Lakers’ injury report, Cameron Carr (right oblique strain) is no longer listed However, Adou Thiero (left knee injury management) remains out and Ziaire Williams (left foot injury management) is questionable. As for the Raptors, Leonard (left knee injury management) won’t be ready to go while Nate Bittle (right avulsion fracture) is out. You can follow Nicole on Twitter at @nicoleganglan i .

stories.title: Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. becomes NBA's first teenager to make 9 3-pointers in a game
stories.summary: Darius Acuff Jr. has been busy in his first couple of weeks of NBA action.
stories.detailText: Darius Acuff Jr. has been busy in his first couple weeks of NBA action. The Sacramento Kings rookie made history Saturday against the Memphis Grizzlies, posting 38 points on 12-of-25 shooting with 5 rebounds and 5 assists. His nine 3-pointers made, out of 14 attempts, tied the NBA single-game rookie record and are the most ever by a teenager . It was his second straight 30-point game and his third in six career games. Darius Acuff Jr. vs. Memphis tonight: 🔥 38 points (game-high) 🔥 9 triples (ties NBA rookie record) Acuff Jr. (19y, 349d) becomes the youngest player in Kings franchise history to record consecutive 30-PT games... surpassing Oscar Robertson (21y, 357d)! pic.twitter.com/d4XXRF0bEH — NBA (@NBA) November 1, 2026 Unfortunately, that performance was a bright spot in an otherwise dull night for the Kings, who lost 136-105 to the Grizzlies. On the other side, Acuff's fellow rookie, Cameron Boozer, led Memphis with 27 points on 8-of-14 shooting with 9 rebounds, 3 assists and 7 turnovers. The Kings are now 0-6, while the Grizzlies are 6-0. Acuff and Boozer are both notable members of one of the most hyped NBA rookie classes in recent memory. Sacramento took Acuff seventh overall after an All-America season at Arkansas in which he also earned SEC Player of the Year honors and the Bob Cousy Award as the nation's best point guard. The Kings might be trending toward another miserable season after going 22-60 last time around, but a strong rookie season for Acuff would make up for plenty of losses when evaluating the team's future.

He is shooting 43.0% from the field and 18.5% from beyond the arc. He has been struggling from the perimeter but the Celtics shouldn’t understimate him and leave him open since he shot 34.5% from three last season. The Celtics need to defend him for both the shot and the pass. Jordan Walsh vs Desmond Bane Bane is averaging 17.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 4.0 assists. He is shooting 33.8% from the field and 33.3% from beyond the arc. He is capable of putting up big numbers if not defended well. In a game against the Celtics last season, he finished with 22 points, 6 rebounds, 7 assists, 1 steal and 2 blocks while shooting 53.3% from the field and 40% from beyond the arc. As with Wagner, the Celtics need to defend him well. Honorable Mention Neemias Queta vs Wendell Carter, Jr. Carter is averaging 14.8 points, 8.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists, and 1.2 steals per game. He is shooting 65.0% from the field and 38.5% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to defend him both in the paint and on the perimeter as he is shooting well from both. Since Robinson is out for rest, we may see Queta or Garza, or even Cenac getting the start. I’m guessing Queta. Keys to the Game Defense – As always, defense is the key to winning this, and every, game. In the preseason, the Celtics were tops in the league with a defensive rating of 98.6. The Celtics are 10th in the league with a 108.1 defensive rating. The Magic are 25th with a defensive rating of 117.0. The Celtics need to continue to play tough defense and make that their identity and priority. Rebound – As with defense, rebounding will always be a key to winning. The Celtics have to crash the boards as a team and go after every rebound. In the preseason, the Celtics were 1st with 55 rebounds per game and 3rd with 16.8 offensive rebounds per game. So far in the regular season, they are 19th in rebounding with 43.6 rebounds per game and 13th with 12.2 offensive rebounds per game. The Magic are 29th with 39.4 rebounds per game. The Celtics are 23rd in the league with 13.8 second chance points per game. The Celtics need to be aggressive on the boards and win the rebounding battle. Effort and Focus for 48 Minutes – The Celtics have to play with extra effort overall for all 4 quarters. In the first half against the Bulls, the Celtics played hard and stayed focused, taking care of the ball and taking and making good shots. In the second half, the Bulls were the team that played harder and the Celtics lost focus on both ends of the court, allowing the Bulls to cut a 29 point lead to 14. The Celtics have to play hard and stay focused for all 48 minutes. Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics need to move the ball to get the best shots. The Celtics are much better when they move the ball and don’t lapse into iso ball. But, they have to be careful with the ball and avoid turnovers. The Celtics are 14th with 15.8 turnovers per game. That is too many. The Magic are averaging 15.6 points off turnovers per game. The Celtics need to make the extra pass to find the best shot but they also need to stay focused and make careful passes. X-Factors Road Game – The Celtics are playing on the road. They are facing distractions of travel and playing in an unfamiliar arena in front of hostile fans. Although, there is often a large contingent of Celtics fans in the arena. They need to shake off those distractions and keep their focus on playing the game. Young players often struggle more on the road and so the young Celtics have to stay focused and try to ignore the distractions. Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. Every crew officiates differently. Some call it tight, others let them play. The Celtics need to adjust to how the refs are calling the game and not allow bad calls or no calls to take away their focus from playing the game. The Celtics also have to be aware of the new points of emphasis for this season and try to avoid off‑arm push‑offs, reckless closeouts, delays before free throws illegal screens and especially flopping. Paul George was already fined for a flop in the first game and there have been several other flopping calls as well.

The Clippers are coming to Chase looking for a fresh start, and Golden State has a chance to remind them who ended the last one.

teamStories.title: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama notches 43 points on career-high 34 shots in win
teamStories.summary: Victor Wembanyama launched a career-high 34 shots for a season-high 43 points to propel the Spurs to a 121-111 win over the Timberwolves.
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs star Victor Wembanyama launched a career-high 34 shots for a season-high 43 points Saturday to propel San Antonio to a 121-111 win over the Timberwolves . "When he plays with his teammates, it really causes a problem for the other team, whether that's spacing, handling the basketball, playing two-man game or three-man game," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "The best players in this league, when they play with their teammates, it's damn near impossible at times [to stop]. You've got to just choose how they beat you. He's made some fine improvement in a short amount of time." Wembanyama's performance marked the first time the Spurs emerged victorious on a night the Frenchman finished with 30 attempts or more. The 22-year-old also contributed five blocks to become the first Spurs player since David Robinson (1996) to rack up at least 40 points and five blocks in a game and the first player in the NBA since Joel Embiid (2022) to accomplish the feat. San Antonio fell short the two previous times Wembanyama hoisted 30 shots or more. He attempted 31 shots on Christmas Day of his second NBA season (2024) to finish with 42 points in a 117-114 loss to the New York Knicks . Four days later, Wembanyama finished with 30 attempts in a 112-110 loss to the Timberwolves. "He's just so dominant," said second-year guard Dylan Harper , who notched a regular-season career-high 25 points on 9-of-17 shooting. "When he puts his imprint on the game, he's unstoppable. He did that tonight from the jump to the end of the game." Wembanyama's shot diet looked different too. He nailed a corner 3-pointer with 2:40 remaining for his final bucket to extend San Antonio's lead to 118-107. Wembanyama would fire up eight 3-pointers on the night, knocking down three of them. But 12 of Wembanyama's 14 other baskets came from distances of two feet or fewer, including four alley-oops and four dunks. Wembanyama mentioned after struggling in San Antonio's season-opening loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder that he needed "to go back to playing the basketball I like." By the 5:23 mark of the third quarter, the "WemVP" chants started raining down on Wembanyama as he took a pair of foul shots. "It's like pattern recognition," he said. "The brain, after so many games, literally hundreds of games now in the NBA, knows what kind of game to go towards to have fun. Because whenever we don't score, it's like negative feedback. Whenever we score, we get good results, positive feedback for the brain. Over time, you recognize patterns, and you err towards those patterns. There's always ups and downs, but we're turning in the right direction." San Antonio's four-guard starting lineup featuring Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle , Devin Vassell and Harper continues to make progress. Wembanyama, Fox and Harper combined for 90 points as the Spurs won the rebounding battle 49-38. Castle finished with four assists and a steal despite fighting through a migraine headache during his 22 minutes on the floor. Wembanyama declined to divulge what's exactly behind his increased comfort level lately, saying "it will help my opponents" to openly discuss. The Frenchman has dropped 36 and 43 points in his last two outings, as the Spurs extended their winning streak to four games. On Saturday, San Antonio faced a depleted Timberwolves team missing star guard Anthony Edwards (knee). LaMelo Ball played only 20 minutes, and he picked up four fouls in the first half before fouling out with 3:43 remaining.

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX -OCTOBER 31: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs blocks shot from Jonathan Kuminga #24 of the Minnesota Timberwolves in the first half at Frost Bank Center on October 31: 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Antonio Spurs still have lessons to be learned. Last season, the Spurs made it pretty far on talent. They would make silly mistakes after silly mistakes and still recover thanks to one of the most talented young rosters in the NBA. After a crushing NBA Finals loss, a lot of fans expected the team to grow up a bit. To learn the lessons that come with such a defeat. Six games into the 2026-27 NBA season, that doesn’t appear to be the case. The Spurs looked almost identical to last year’s team in a 121-111 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves on Halloween night. There were stretches of brilliance when the team guarded like their lives depended on it, moved the ball on a string, and got to the cup with ease. Then there were times when the offense went completely cold, reliant on isolation ball, and the defense allowed second-chance points and easy transition looks. But ultimately, the Spurs had enough talent to take down a Minnesota team that was missing two key players in Anthony Edwards and Rudy Gobert. It took an MVP performance to get the win. Victor Wembanyama took over the game, crushing his fellow countryman, Joan Beringer, with 43 points and 6 blocks. When San Antonio was in a slog, Wembanyama would pull them out with a well-timed dunk or a block that led to a transition runout. Those are the types of games you’re looking for from the face of the franchise and potentially the best player in the league. As they say, a win is a win. But likely, Mitch Johnson and the rest of the Spurs’ coaching staff will identify plenty of areas where the team can clean up their game, just as they could last season. Takeaways: Was there some sort of Halloween slime, or perhaps LaMelo Ball’s spit , on the basketball on Saturday? Both teams combined for 29 turnovers, with the ball generally bouncing all over the place. Both teams were trying to play with such a chaotic pace in both transition and half-court offense that it led to a lot of mistakes, or the ball slipping off players’ hands and bodies. We at Pounding the Rock are formally accepting De’Aaron Fox apology slips. We will forward them to Mr. Fox at our earliest convenience. The veteran point guard has been nothing short of the Spurs’ second-best player to begin the season. He had 22 points, 8 rebounds, and 7 assists in the win, and was a team-high +23. Whatever he did in the offseason worked, because he looks completely rejuvenated. His jump shot is falling, particularly in the mid-range, which is opening up a lot of offense for the Spurs. San Antonio has figured out how to constantly get the ball to Wembanyama on lobs. Those short pick-and-rolls near the sideline make it hard for opposing bigs to drop back and protect the rim, as it gives the Spurs’ guards good angles at the rim. That forced Beringer to switch often on Saturday night, making it easy for Wembanyama to finish lobs over smaller defenders. It’s one of the best new wrinkles to San Antonio’s playbook, and they spammed it often against Minnesota. Luke Kornet has gotten a lot of grief for his play this season, and a lot of it has been deserved. He should get some praise when he has a solid game, too. Kornet grabbed 8 rebounds, 4 of them offensive, including a big put-back slam in the first half. His defensive positioning was largely good, and he didn’t kill San Antonio when he was in the game. That is about all you can ask from a backup center in this league. Julian Champagnie remains red hot from three-point range to start the season. He shot 3-of-7 from deep on his way to 12 points against the Wolves and is now shooting 47.6% from three to start the season. It’s about time that Champagnie gets the recognition for what he is: one of the best shooters in the NBA.

(Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Antonio Spurs delivered the tricks and took home the treat on Halloween, earning a 121–111 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves at the Frost Bank Center on Saturday night, sending the fans home with smiles on their faces and candy in their bellies. The victory is the fourth straight for San Antonio, who started the season 0-2 after losses to the Oklahoma City Thunder and the Houston Rockets. Spurs Head Coach Mitch Johnson informed reporters before the game that guard Stephon Castle was suffering from a migraine and was a game-time decision. He would eventually be in the starting lineup and play 22 minutes. San Antonio opened the game with one of their strongest defensive efforts of the season, holding the Timberwolves to 37 percent shooting in the first quarter. At one point in the period, the Spurs led 11-2, but the Timberwolves went on an 11-0 run to briefly take a one-point lead. De’Aaron Fox and Victor Wembanyama combined for 19 of the Spurs’ 34 points. “We want to just try to make sure we can get the best shot in every possession, and that’s never going to happen,” Coach Johnson said after the game. “But I think if you just constantly keep that at the front of your brain and at the at the forefront of the conversation, and if everybody, for the most part, over time is putting their energy into that, you’ll land in a pretty good spot.” Wembanayama knew he needed to be more aggressive and he acted like it. From the opening tip, he was calling for Fox, Dylan Harper, and Stephon Castle to lob him the ball. He scored 24 points in the first half (43 points for the game), including throwing the ball to himself off the glass for a dunk that got the crowd on its feet and had Minnesota head coach Chris Finch asking for a timeout. “He’s just so dominant,” Harper said of Wembanyama. “I feel like he goes out there and when he puts his imprint on the game, he’s unstoppable, and he did that tonight from the jump to end of the game. So I mean, hey, I was okay with him taking those shots. Those are all good looks, and my biggest thing with him is just if you’re gonna take the shot, take it, be confident.” San Antonio went up double digits, but turnovers allowed the Timberwolves to get back into the game, turning the deficit for Minnesota into a one-point lead at halftime. The Spurs committed four their 15 turnovers in the second quarter. With Minnesota missing stars Anthony Edwards, Rudy Golbert, and Donte DiVincenzo, Finch relied on newly acquired guard LaMelo Ball. The new Minnesota guard saw himself in foul trouble, racking up four personal fouls in the first half. He would eventually foul out of the game, finishing with 10 points and eight rebounds. The final quarter saw the Spurs turn it on, leaving no doubt on which team would go home with the treat of a win on Halloween. San Antonio outscored Minnesota 28-23 in the period, led by Wembanyama, Dylan Harper, and De’Aaron Fox. The sophomore guard finished with 25 points, seven rebounds, and six assists as he got aggressive with Wemby on the bench to begin the period. “I love games like this,” Harper said after the game. “I love games where the other team starts talking first because when you respond, it’s not your fault when you talk.. the competitive nature that the Timberwolves brought kind of brings the best out of us. And obviously, when a team’s that competitive, it brings the best out of me.” De’Aaron Fox had a solid outing, including hitting key shots when Minnesota threatened to come back. He finished with 22 points, eight rebounds, and seven assists; crediting Wembanyama for making everyone better. “His gravity is like Steph (Curry),” Fox said. “If he rolls to the basket, he’s going to have two or three defenders. To use that gravity, makes it easier for the rest of us.” Game Notes Luke Kornet had a strong outing after a string of poor games. He finished with 2 points and 8 rebounds, including four offensive boards. Carter Bryant came off the bench and hit two threes. He played with confidence and that’s a welcome sign. San Antonio will need to cut back on the turnovers, but they made up for it with solid defense in the final two quarters. Julian Champaignie had 12 points off the bench, going 3-f0r-7 from beyond the arc. Coach Johnson said pregame that the team will not rush Tobias Harris back to the court amid all the gruesome injury news around the league over the past week. I’d expect it to be a few weeks until he makes his debut.

stories.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson out for game with thumb injury suffered on 1st play
stories.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Bills with a right thumb injury.
stories.detailText: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Lamar Jackson 's return lasted one play. Jackson, the star quarterback for the Baltimore Ravens , was ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills with a right thumb injury. He hurt his thumb on his first play in Sunday's game. While throwing a pass, Jackson had his right hand struck by the hand of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau , who was attempting to knock down the throw. The two-time NFL MVP immediately looked down at his hand and went to the sideline. He went into the tunnel with his right hand wrapped and held by a trainer. It only got worse for the Ravens in the second quarter, when Tyler "Snoop" Huntley , who was 2-for-4 for zero yards, left the game with a right toe injury. Huntley was ruled out in the third quarter. With Jackson and Huntley injured, Baltimore turned to No. 3 quarterback Joe Fagnano , an undrafted rookie out of Connecticut . Fagnano, who made his first regular-season appearance after an impressive preseason, finished the game 10 of 21 passing for 91 yards and an interception. This was Jackson's first game back after missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain. It's a devastating loss for Baltimore, which had scored only five touchdowns in the previous 14 quarters without Jackson. Jackson returned to the sideline in the third quarter with what appeared to be a brace on his right hand. It's been nine years since a team has had this run of injuries at quarterback this early in a game. The last time a team had three quarterbacks throw a pass in a first half was the 2017 Dallas Cowboys . The Ravens (4-3) are looking to avoid a three-game losing streak.

stories.title: Inside the complicated injury history of Ravens' Lamar Jackson
stories.summary: If the QB's health record has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be challenging.
stories.detailText: Lamar Jackson 's 2026 season is turning into the most injury-filled one of his nine-year career. Jackson missed three games with a high left ankle sprain and returned only to injure his right thumb on his first snap of Sunday's game at the Buffalo Bills . If Jackson's injury history has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be complicated and an extended absence can derail the Ravens' season. But ultimately, the only one who truly knows when Jackson will return is Jackson himself. "Look, if he's able to play, [is] healthy enough to play and play the way that obviously we feel like he needs to play, then he will play," coach Jesse Minter said Monday. Two weeks ago, there was a feeling within the team that Jackson was going to be able to play last Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals . He practiced as a limited participant all week, worked with the first-team offense that Friday and took part in the television production meetings, which usually signifies he will be the starting quarterback. But Jackson was ruled out last Saturday after he experienced increased swelling in his injured left ankle, according to a report during the CBS game broadcast. Tracy Wolfson, the sideline reporter for Sunday's game, posted on social media that it "came as a shock to the Ravens that Lamar couldn't go." Minter later said that was "a little bit" of a mischaracterization. In his first comments since getting injured two weeks ago, Jackson made it clear last week that the decision to play comes down to pain tolerance. It still hurts for Jackson to plant his foot when running. "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play," Jackson said. "But [if] I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, [then] I'm not helping [anybody]. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all." Jackson has now missed multiple games because of injury in four of his past six seasons, but it's a flawed narrative to describe him as the NFL's most injured quarterback. Jackson, who has been sidelined for 17 games with injuries (excluding COVID and illness), has missed fewer games than four other starting quarterbacks -- Kyler Murray (31), Dak Prescott (26), Daniel Jones (25) and Joe Burrow (22) -- since 2019. "It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback that kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said earlier this month. "I feel like you just don't see these same articles, and you don't see these same headlines. I think it's unfair treatment." Humphrey added, "I just feel like it goes -- sometimes it seems like it gets away from -- I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him. I do know this: If Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play." When Jackson misses time, it can turn the Ravens from a championship contender to a team struggling to make the postseason. In the three seasons in which he has missed at least four games, Baltimore failed to make the playoffs twice (2021 and 2025). This season, Jackson started off strong and looked like an MVP candidate in his first four games. He ranked third in QBR (82.7), throwing six touchdowns and one interception. Jackson also led all quarterbacks with 144 yards rushing. After Jackson sprained his ankle, the Ravens went from being atop the AFC North at 3-1 to falling to last place in the division at 4-3 heading into Sunday's game against the Bills. Minter said Jackson was in a "decent spot" health-wise entering this week. "Lamar is one of one, right? [He's a] two-time MVP, obviously a high-caliber player," Minter said. "But I just don't like the built-in excuse of why things are going a certain way. So, while we know the caliber of player Lamar is and the numbers when he's out there versus when he's not, we understand all that. That's why he's who he is and why he's won the awards that he's won, but we can still operate better in those times where we don't have him, for sure." 2026: High ankle sprain and right thumb For the first time in his career, Jackson could miss multiple game in one season due to two injuries. After missing three games with a high left ankle sprain, Jackson returned only to leave after one snap with another injury. He hurt his right thumb when his hand collided with the hand of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau. The timetable for Jackson's latest injury is unknown. 2025: Hamstring In late September, Jackson left midway through the third quarter of a loss at the Kansas City Chiefs after being sacked by defensive end George Karlaftis and did not return. He sat on the bench for the remainder of the game, occasionally flexing his injured right leg. Jackson was out for the next three games, but not without a misunderstanding. After Jackson's second missed game, Baltimore originally listed Jackson as a full participant in a Friday practice before changing his practice status to limited a day later because he ran only the scout team. The Ravens then ruled out Jackson. After returning, Jackson never looked at full strength the rest of the year. He was 8-5 as the starter for the remainder of the season, throwing 17 touchdown passes and seven interceptions. Jackson also chose not to run as much, averaging 25 yards rushing in the final 13 games. This month, Jackson expressed regret for coming back too quickly from that hamstring injury. "I feel like that was dumb a little bit," Jackson said. Almost exactly a year later, the Ravens are in waiting mode again for Jackson. "I think when Lamar and our training staff and our doctors and myself and everybody in the organization feel that it's best for him to be on the field, that he'll be on the field," Minter said, "and everybody will know when that is." 2022: Sprained knee In early December, Jackson was hurt on the last play of the first quarter when he was sacked from behind by linebacker Jonathon Cooper . It looked like Jackson's left knee was driven into the ground when Cooper landed on top of his back. Jackson sprained his PCL, but Harbaugh announced it wasn't a season-ending injury. "We'll see if he can go back this week," Harbaugh said after the game. "If not, it'll be sometime after that shortly." It turned out to be a season-ending injury for Jackson, who missed the final five regular-season games as well as the wild-card game in Cincinnati. Ravens officials were confident that Jackson would return for the postseason until Jackson posted on social media three days before the game. He explained his left knee "remains unstable" and that his injury is more serious than originally believed. Jackson indicated that he has "suffered a PCL Grade 2 sprain, on the borderline of a strain 3." "I wish I could be out there with my guys more than anything, but I can't give a 100% of myself to my guys and fans," Jackson wrote. "I'm still hopeful we have a chance." The Ravens lost to the Bengals 24-17 when backup Tyler Huntley 's fumble on a quarterback sneak at the goal line turned into a 98-yard winning touchdown return for Cincinnati. 2021: Ankle injury Five years ago, Jackson suffered the first significant injury of his NFL career when he was carted off the field in Cleveland in December. In trying to escape the pocket on a pass play, Jackson went down to the ground after Browns linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah dove at Jackson's heels. Jackson sustained a bone bruise on his right ankle that wasn't considered serious at first. After the season, then-Ravens coach John Harbaugh said, "The first week, he thought he had a chance. The second week, he assured me, he said, 'I'll be back. I'll be back.'" Jackson ended up missing the final four games, all of which resulted in losses. Baltimore went from leading the AFC North at 8-5 to failing to earn a playoff berth. "Those things are really unpredictable," Harbaugh said.

stories.title: NFL Week 8 Winners and Losers: Lamar Jackson's thumb injury could lead to a sad ending for him and Ravens
stories.summary: The Ravens could be without their quarterback for a while due to another injury.
stories.detailText: It's stunning to think that the Baltimore Ravens could have almost a decade of one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time and not make the Super Bowl once. But it might be headed that way. The Lamar Jackson era was summed up fairly well Sunday. Jackson was back from an ankle injury. The two-time MVP's return brought hope that he could lift the Ravens back to being a Super Bowl contender, starting with a win at the Buffalo Bills. One offensive play in, all that hope was gone. Jackson suffered a thumb injury following through on a pass on the Ravens' first play on offense. He went to the locker room and was ruled out shortly after. Lamar Jackson heads to the locker room after his first pass attempt with an apparent hand injury. pic.twitter.com/JVUQYjJV8H — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 1, 2026 Jackson was on the sideline for the second half with a black brace on his right hand. By the time he returned to the sideline he was watching undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano make his NFL debut, after Tyler Huntley left with a toe injury. Baltimore fell to 4-4 with a 36-10 loss to the Bills. Normally a .500 record at the beginning of November wouldn’t be the end of anyone’s season but it seems like it for Baltimore after Sunday. The Ravens defense tried to keep the team in the game against the Bills for as long as it could but there was simply no offense without Jackson. That will be the case going forward, and it seems like Jackson could miss a significant amount of time. When Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb earlier this season he missed three games. Jackson has taken his time coming back from injuries, a truth that has been frustrating in Baltimore, and that has to be accounted for. By the time he's back, the Ravens might be well out of the AFC North race. And if it was just one game against the Bills, or even a few weeks going forward, the mood might be different. But it's way more than that. Jackson is in his ninth season with the Ravens, and the dream of an exciting era having a satisfying conclusion might be fading fast. Jackson has one year left on a five-year, $260 million contract extension. Multiple media reports have said there have been no recent negotiations. Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti said in January he didn't want the contract issue dragging into April, and now it's November. Both sides have said they want the relationship to continue but it's way more complicated than it was when he was given the franchise tag in 2023 and he came back on a huge deal. Jackson will turn 30 in January. Injuries are becoming a big part of his story. Given how much he relies on his mobility, his game might not age well into his 30s. There was also a scathing piece by the Baltimore Sun after last season that reshaped the Jackson narrative, painting him as a player who is difficult to work with. Everything is more convoluted with Jackson's future than it was a few years ago. It's especially hard to navigate because of how good Jackson is. He's a three-time first-team All-Pro, entered Sunday's games second all time in passer rating while also being the greatest running quarterback ever. The Ravens can entertain trading him — if they don't want to go forward with Jackson after 2027 they'd have to make that move to recoup some value — but everyone knows the chances of finding a quarterback who can be as good as Jackson are almost zero. Seeing Baltimore struggle with Huntley and Fagnano at quarterback gives the Ravens a look at what the future could be without Jackson, and the floor is very low. But if this season goes south, it seems more and more likely that a divorce is on the table next offseason. The story of this season hasn't been written yet. Assuming Jackson returns, there's a chance to set up a totally different ending. And, perhaps he and the Ravens simply come to a contract extension like they did last time. It's not like the Ravens have a succession plan in place. But with one play in Buffalo on Sunday, Jackson's future with the Ravens, what comes next for Baltimore and the ripple effects of those decisions around the NFL became the focus. It seemed like a turning point, and not a good one for anyone involved. Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 8 of the NFL season: WINNERS The 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers: The Steelers started the season by squeezing out close wins. As the weeks go on, they’re started to look better. The Cleveland Browns are not the litmus test, despite their 5-2 record coming into Sunday’s game. Cleveland still has a bad quarterback situation and can’t live off last-second wins all season. Still, the Steelers left no doubt, which is the sign of a good team. They blasted the Browns 27-6. . @Nunless2 having a DAY‼️ pic.twitter.com/2gsIq0MUTe — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 Everything was positive. The Steelers defense played very well. The running game was fantastic again with Jaylen Warren leading the way. Aaron Rodgers was efficient during a game in which he didn’t need to do much. The Steelers have a sterling record and are getting better. That’s a sign of good coaching. Mike McCarthy is off to a fine start to his Pittsburgh career. Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers played like a service academy team on Sunday, giving up on the passing game altogether in the rain. It was OK because Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell were fantastic in a 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers didn’t complete a pass, but Irving had 170 rushing yards and a touchdown and Gainwell added 140 more. Bucky Irving TD! He's up to 169 yards! ATLvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PsIV3YPlxE — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 it was the first time since 1974 that a team won without a completion. The Buffalo Bills pulled that off in the rain and heavy wind with Joe Ferguson completing 0-of-2 passes. There were completions to Buccaneers, but they came from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. Penix threw four interceptions. Penix struggled in the conditions, while the Buccaneers didn’t even try to throw it. The running game was enough for the Buccaneers’ second straight win. The NFC South is bad again, so even a team that started 1-5 and has completed fewer than 10 passes the past two weeks should still have legitimate hope of winning the division. Kirk Cousins: Every week, Cousins might be playing for his job. After the Las Vegas Raiders had a four-game losing streak it seemed like a change could be made. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said last Sunday everything would be considered, including a quarterback change, though he walked that back the next day. Cousins will keep his job at least another week. Cousins played very well, throwing for three touchdowns and getting another on a quarterback sneak as the Raiders beat the New York Jets 38-33. The Raiders allowed the Jets to score on their first six possessions, but the offense was good enough to overcome that. Cousins was very good, and smart in targeting Brock Bowers repeatedly. Bowers had 92 yards and two touchdowns. Cousins even got in a celebration after the touchdown, though he looked very much like a 38-year-old quarterback doing it. Kirko wyd? pic.twitter.com/WxkoNvm4Ge — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 At some point this season, top overall pick Fernando Mendoza is very likely to start. But it won’t be right away, after Cousins had a superb game. LOSERS Jonathan Taylor: The Indianapolis Colts probably should have just deactivated Taylor on Sunday. There wasn’t much point in playing him. The Colts are in for a rough finish to the season. After trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner this week, the Colts were wholly uncompetitive in a 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. They trailed 28-0 at halftime. It’s the kind of loss that could lead the team to fire Shane Steichen, even if they were seemingly trying to get through the rest of the season with him. The effort from the defense on multiple Jaguars touchdowns was severely lacking. It was an utterly embarrassing performance for the entire franchise. Bhayshul Tuten ends the 3rd quarter with his 2nd TD! @Jaguars are in the 40s! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ShxRF0caiJ — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Taylor is the one big trade piece left, and the story will unfold one of two ways before the deadline: Taylor’s fantastic career with the Colts will come to an end with the teams in tatters, or he’ll continue to play with a team that might only win a game or two the rest of the season if they can muster a win at all. For Taylor’s sake he will get dealt, because the rest of the Colts’ season will be depressing. Vikings offense: Finally, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense couldn’t save the day. The Vikings should have been able to score plenty against a questionable Detroit Lions defense, but were able to put up 15 points. The defense held strong until Jameson Williams scored a go-ahead touchdown in the final five minutes, and the Vikings’ offense couldn’t answer. Detroit won 19-15, meaning there are no undefeated teams left this season. JAMESON WILLIAMS TD MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/b87aoClNR0 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Vikings have been great on offense and questionable on offense all season. It didn’t matter for the first six games, which were all wins. Kyler Murray wasn’t the problem on Sunday but he wasn’t great either, with 210 passing yards against a defense that has been giving up a ton of points and yards this season. At some point if the Vikings want to win the NFC North they’ll need some more offensive punch. It’s still lacking. And it will really get uncomfortable in Minnesota if J.J. McCarthy, who they traded a few weeks ago, continues to play well with the Giants.

The Jaguars rolled to a 28-0 halftime lead at home and then kept pounding the Colts in the second half until they finally called off the dogs in the fourth quarter. The 42-7 win moves the Jags to 5-2 on the season and they got to rest starters in the final minutes as they started thinking about Thursday's game in Baltimore. It looked for a moment like the Colts might be able to make it a game when Jaylahn Tuimoloau forced a Trevor Lawrence fumble on a sack, but their scoring chances went up in smoke when Daniel Jones was picked off by Rayuan Lane on a pass that went off tight end Tyler Warren's hands. One question was answered in the fourth when the Colts pulled Jones after his second interception and gave Anthony Richardson his first chance to play this season. The Jaguars don't have to wonder about trading players away and they may be more interested in adding to a roster that has them well on their way to another division title. Bhayshul Tuten had 159 yards of offense and two touchdowns while Lawrence was an efficient 10-of-14 for 210 yards and three scores before letting Quinn Ewers get some time on offense. One of Lawrence's touchdowns went to Brian Thomas, who had not caught a pass of any kind since Week 4, and there were nothing but smiles on the Jacksonville sideline at the end of this one.

stories.title: Goff throws go-ahead touchdown pass to Williams and Lions beat Vikings 19-15 for their 1st loss
stories.summary: — Jared Goff threw a go-ahead, 7-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams with 4:35 left and the Detroit Lions beat the Minnesota Vikings 19-15 on...
stories.detailText: DETROIT -- — Jared Goff threw a go-ahead, 7-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams with 4:35 left and the Detroit Lions beat the Minnesota Vikings 19-15 on Sunday, handing the NFL's last undefeated team its first loss. The Lions (5-2) have won three straight, including their first two division games in the tight NFC North. The Vikings (6-1) had a chance to stay unbeaten, but the league's stingiest defense couldn't hold onto a late lead, and they lost for the first time since Nov. 30, 2025, at Seattle. Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards, including a 30-yard, tackle-breaking touchdown in the third quarter. Goff was 18 of 25 for 176 yards with a touchdown and his first interception of the season. Kyler Murray was 17 of 29 for 210 yards with two touchdown and an interception, leading an offensively challenged team that had just 81 yards rushing. The Lions broke a scoreless tie late in the first quarter on Jake Bates ' 25-yard field goal after their star receivers — Amon Ra-St. Brown and Williams — stunted the first two drives with taunting penalties St. Brown had a chance to make up for his flag with a touchdown catch, but the play was reversed after a review that showed he didn't secure the football as he fell after making a reception with his fingertips and getting both feet in the end zone. The Vikings went ahead 7-3 early in the second quarter when Murray lofted a 1-yard pass to the left side of the end zone that Justin Jefferson snagged with his left hand before going to the turf and completing the catch. Lions cornerback D.J. Reed , who broke up a pass in the end zone on the game's first drive, cut in front of Jordan Addison to make a diving interception late in the second quarter. Detroit, huddling up and taking time off the clock on its last drive of the first half, converted a fourth-and-1 from its 47 and Bates later made a 37-yard field goal to make it 7-6. With a chance to take the lead early in the third, Bates' 46-yard kick hit the left upright. The Vikings had a chance to put points on the board in the second half from the Detroit 25, but coach Kevin O'Connell went for it on fourth-and-5 and Murray threw an incomplete pass. Murray threw an 8-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson and a 2-point conversion pass to Jordan Addison for a 15-12 lead midway through the fourth quarter. Minnesota's defense, though, could not hold onto the lead. Injuries Vikings: Safety Theo Jackson (quad) was injured during the game. Lions: Linebacker Jack Campbell was placed on a backboard, carted off the field in the fourth quarter and taken to a hospital with a neck injury. Safety Brian Branch and edge DJ Wonnum were evaluated for concussions after colliding late in the second quarter and didn't return. Up next Vikings: Host the Bills on Monday, Nov. 9. Lions: at Miami on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Bucs down Falcons without pass completion; Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell run wild
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield didn't complete a pass but the Buccaneers beat the Falcons 16-0 behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell's rushing on a wet, sloppy field.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, Fla. -- Baker Mayfield didn't complete a pass but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 on Sunday behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell 's rushing on a wet, sloppy field. The Buccaneers (3-5) set a team record for yards rushing in a game with 324, and became the first team to have zero completions since Buffalo on Sept. 29, 1974. The Bills beat the Jets 16-12 in that one, and that had been the only time a team didn't complete a pass in the Super Bowl era. Irving ran for 170 yards and one touchdown on 27 carries, Gainwell ran for 140 on 25 carries. Before Sunday, there had never been a game in NFL history where two teammates both had at least 25 rushing attempts and 125 rushing yards. Also, Chase McLaughlin kicked three field goals to stay perfect this season at 19 for 19. Playing in a driving rain for most of the afternoon, Mayfield was 0 for 3 in his second game back after missing three weeks with a fractured thumb. Tampa Bay finished with minus-2 net passing yards thanks to a sack. It got got 100.6% of its offensive yards on the ground (324 of 322). Michael Penix Jr . went 8 for 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions for Atlanta (3-5). Bijan Robinson was held to 76 yards on 19 carries. Mayfield and Kevin Stefanski are the only QB-coach combination to win a playoff game for the Browns in the 2000s but they didn't have a close relationship. Mayfield was upset that Stefanski didn't reach out to him after the Browns traded him to Carolina in 2022. Facing Stefanski and the Falcons on Sunday, Mayfield didn't have to do much with his arm. He scrambled for 13 yards while Irving and Gainwell piled up big numbers. Tampa Bay's previous rushing high was 283 yards -- including 235 from Doug Martin -- in a 45-17 win at Philadelphia on Nov. 22, 2015. Irving's 4-yard TD run in the third quarter gave the Buccaneers a 16-0 lead and the offense kept pounding the ball on the ground. Nick Folk missed a 53-yard field goal wide left on Atlanta's opening series and McLaughlin made one from 46 yards out on the next series. The Bucs missed an opportunity after Alex Anzalone picked off Penix at Atlanta's 41 and returned it 8 yards, and an unsportsmanlike penalty on Drake London put the ball at the 18. But Irving fumbled out of the end zone for a touchback after taking a lateral from Mayfield. Jessie Bates III forced the fumble. Anzalone picked off Penix again on Atlanta's next possession to set up Tampa Bay at the Falcons 19. But the Buccaneers couldn't go anywhere and settled for McLaughlin's 34-yarder that made it 6-0. After Jacob Parrish picked off Penix on a fourth-down pass at Tampa Bay's 17, the Buccaneers drove 65 yards and McLaughlin connected from 42 yards to extend the lead to 9-0. Last week, Tampa Bay beat the Panthers 43-13 with Mayfield completing just 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards. The Bucs have won three of four since an 0-4 start and are just a half-game behind Carolina (3-4) in the NFC South. In the Jets-Bills game in 1974, Joe Ferguson was 0 for 2 for Buffalo, O.J. Simpson ran for 117 yards and Ferguson and Jim Braxton each had rushing touchdowns. New York's Joe Namath completed just 2 of 18 passes for 33 yards. Information from ESPN Research and The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.title: Vikings' reign as NFL's last undefeated team comes to end with loss to Lions
stories.summary: The Vikings' reign as the NFL's lone remaining undefeated team is over, as Minnesota fell to the Lions on Sunday.
stories.detailText: The NFL's last unbeaten team has fallen. The Minnesota Vikings saw their unblemished start come to an end Sunday, Nov. 1, falling in a 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions . The Vikings' defense once again created havoc for the team's NFC North rival in the early going, with the unit bagging Lions quarterback Jared Goff for four sacks. But Detroit broke through in the second half with two touchdown drives. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who finished with 153 rushing yards on 23 carries, scored the first touchdown when he broke free on a 30-yard jaunt in the third quarter. Gibbs then powered a fourth-quarter drive that was capped by a 7-yard touchdown connection between Goff and wide receiver Jameson Williams. Outside of wide receiver Justin Jefferson tipping an end zone fade to himself in the second quarter, Minnesota's offense once again struggled to find a spark. The Vikings were outgained 384 yards to 266, and quarterback Kyler Murray generated just 210 yards on 17-of-29 passing. Murray did manage to help the offense come alive in the fourth quarter, when he uncorked a 51-yard deep heave to Jordan Addison. An 8-yard strike temporarily put Minnesota back on top before the Lions regained the lead. Trailing by 4, however, the Vikings went three-and-out. Detroit then salted the game away in the final minutes. Fresh off their first defeat, the Vikings face a difficult road ahead. A "Monday Night Football" matchup with the Buffalo Bills awaits before road matchups with the Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers.
