stories.title: Steelers bulldoze Browns 27-6 to take AFC North lead, extend home streak over rivals to 23 straight
stories.summary: — Jaylen Warren tied a career high with 143 yards rushing and a touchdown on his 28th birthday, and the Pittsburgh Steelers moved into first place in the AFC North by drilling Cleveland 27-6 on...
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- — Jaylen Warren tied a career high with 143 yards rushing and a touchdown on his 28th birthday, and the Pittsburgh Steelers moved into first place in the AFC North by drilling Cleveland 27-6 on Sunday. The Steelers (6-2) avenged a road loss to the Browns (5-3) a month ago by dominating the line of scrimmage and reminding Cleveland that while the years change, the result when the Browns play in Pittsburgh does not. The lopsided result marked the Steelers' 23rd straight regular-season win over their longtime rivals at Acrisure Stadium, tying the NFL record for consecutive home victories over an opponent. Green Bay won 23 in a row against Detroit from 1992 to 2014. The surprising Browns, eyeing their best start in 32 years thanks to the late-game heroics of quarterback Deshaun Watson , came in hoping this time would be different. Defensive end Jared Verse predicted it would be during the week, saying Cleveland would “make Pittsburgh ours.” It didn't quite happen like that. The Steelers sacked Watson eight times, and the Pittsburgh offensive line that Verse openly questioned spent three-plus hours bullying the Browns in general and Verse in particular. The 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year was a nonfactor and at one point landed on his head when Pittsburgh guard Mason McCormick slammed him into the turf during a Steelers field-goal attempt. McCormick was called for unnecessary roughness on the play, but the point had been made. Warren, in the midst of a breakout year, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle ran through gaping holes as the Steelers ran for 200 yards, including 160 in the first half, the most by any team in the opening half this season. Dowdle's 56 yards rushing included a 9-yard sprint up the middle to the end zone in the first quarter that gave Pittsburgh a lead it never came close to squandering. The Steelers scored on four of their next five possessions, including a 1-yard plunge by tight end Pat Freiermuth on a tush push on the penultimate play of the first half that put Pittsburgh up 20-6 at the break. When Aaron Rodgers hit 6-foot-7, 300-pound tight end Darnell Washington for a 58-yard catch-and-rumble early in the third quarter that set up Warren's 1-yard touchdown dive, the Steelers were up by three touchdowns and the late magic Watson summoned five times over the season's first two months was nowhere to be found. Rodgers finished 13 of 25 for 172 yards with a second-half interception courtesy of wide receiver DK Metcalf , who bobbled the ball directly into the hands of Cleveland defensive back Denzel Ward . It was a rare misstep on a day the Steelers — outside of some questionable play-calling deep in Browns territory in the first half — did what they almost always do when their rivals from two hours away pay a visit. Watson, under pressure from the opening possession, passed for 324 yards, many of them in garbage time. He exited briefly in the first quarter after taking a late shot from Pittsburgh's Jaquan Brisker . Shedeur Sanders came in for a couple of chaotic plays, with his stint ending on a fumble by Harold Fannin Jr . The Browns fumbled on their next possession, too, as a script that's become familiar across the decades played out yet again. stories.title: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly, claims Bills franchise passing touchdown record
stories.summary: Allen moves past Hall of Famer Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in Bills history, including the postseason.
stories.detailText: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen has spent much of his career rewriting the Buffalo Bills’ record books. On Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens, he claimed another piece of franchise history, moving past Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Jim Kelly for the most career touchdown passes, including the postseason. Josh Allen connects with DJ Moore on his 259th career passing TD (including playoffs), surpassing Jim Kelly (258) for the most in franchise history. pic.twitter.com/zkxVUT79R9 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 1, 2026 Allen entered the game tied with Kelly at 258 touchdown passes. His 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the fourth quarterback gave him No. 259, putting him alone at the top of a list that Kelly had led since his retirement following the 1996 season. Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Just two weeks earlier, Allen had pulled even with Kelly during Buffalo’s 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. A nine-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Khalil Shakir brought him within one of the record before a 12-yard backhanded shovel pass to wide receiver Keon Coleman tied the two quarterbacks at 258. The record includes both regular-season and postseason touchdowns, a distinction that matters when comparing the two quarterbacks. Kelly still holds Buffalo’s regular-season record with 237 touchdown passes, while Allen entered Sunday’s game with 229. Allen has reached the combined mark considerably faster than his predecessor. Kelly played 177 games over 11 seasons with Buffalo, including 17 postseason appearances. Allen entered the Ravens game having played 149 games, including 15 in the playoffs, putting him 28 games behind Kelly when he matched the Hall of Famer’s total. With half a season still on the calendar, and Allen just needing just eight touchdowns to move his name onto the top line under the title “Franchise leader for regular season touchdown passes,” the watch for Allen to take another category is on.

stories.title: Jaguars Run Indianapolis Out of Duval in Dominant Win
stories.summary: Jacksonville’s 35-point beatdown of Indianapolis extended its home dominance over the Colts to 12 straight wins.
stories.detailText: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Bhayshul Tuten of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs with the ball during the NFL London Series match between Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars entered their 2026 Rivalry Week wearing their sandy beach jerseys for the first time, in front of the Jacksonville home crowd. On the field, the Duval ‘House of Horrors’ continued for the Indianapolis Colts, as Indianapolis failed to make this one even remotely competitive from the opening quarter on, cementing 12 consecutive home wins over the 2-6 Colts. 11 of the 12 wins occurred in Jacksonville, with one taking place in London. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 8 42-7, 35-point domination of the Indianapolis Colts. P lay(s) of the game: Nate Boerkircher’s first touchdown of his rookie season was one of beauty, with the “Consensus Board All Star” locating the ball in flight over his opposite shoulder for the touchdown, extending the lead to two scores. Trevor Lawrence finds a wide open Nate Boerkircher for his 2nd TD pass of the first half! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H3ubmhXBZo — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Post-game notables: Jaguars Backfield Goes Wild Running backs Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez combined for 217 total yards and three touchdowns, as Tuten made his mark in the run and passing game, going 16 carries for 104 yards and a touchdown, with an additional 55 yards and a touchdown in the air. Chris Rodriguez added another 58 total yards and a touchdown. The two backs combined for 145 rushing yards on 22 carries (6.59 per carry), with the game clearly in hand by halftime. A Clean Day Following back-to-back weeks with 13 penalties during weeks five and six, the Jacksonville Jaguars have seemed to correct this early-season issue, with just 6 penalties against the Houston Texans and 7 on Sunday. Travis Hunter: Punt Returner? Early in the first quarter, Jacksonville sent cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter back to return a punt for the first time in the 2026 season. While the team has toyed with this in training camp, it was somewhat shocking to see Parker Washington, a Pro Bowl-caliber punt returner, taken off the field. My question: Is this move more indicative of the value that Washington holds as a wide receiver building block for the future? Or is the move more about finding every opportunity available to get the ball into the hands of the explosive Hunter? Interestingly, the return in question was right after the opening punt return when Indianapolis downed the ball at the two-yard line. Davon Hamilton Loss Looms Huge While the game outcome clearly takes precedence, the wet Duval weather wasn’t the only thing to place a damper on the celebration at EverBank Stadium. The Jacksonville Jaguars dominated their AFC South rival on a rainy Sunday afternoon. However, defensive tackle Davon Hamilton being carted off the field with a first-half knee injury was the immediate focus of many following the final seconds. The league-leading defense at stopping the run losing their dominant nose tackle is certainly news. The immediate question surrounds the severity of Hamilton’s injury, with secondary questions resting on Jacksonville’s options moving forward, with the approaching November 10th trade deadline. Hamilton was carted from the field following the defense’s fumble recovery on the failed trick play. The trick play goes awry and the Jaguars get it back! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AinguLvhQi — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 In-Game Injuries As a note, the following Jacksonville players left Sunday’s game due to injury: DT Davon Hamilton (knee) S Eric Murray (elbow) RG Ezra Cleveland (ankle) DE Travon Walker (ribs) In Case You Missed It The outcome of Sunday’s AFC South matchup seemed extremely clear by the end of the first quarter, after Jacksonville took an early 7-0 lead via a 12-yard Brian Thomas Jr. reception. Brian Thomas Jr. starts the scoring in Jacksonville! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TSkI5R33VG — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Before Indianapolis could blink, it seemed that the score was already out of reach, with explosive scores from Nate Boerkircher and Bhayshul Tuten. However, an Indianapolis opportunity to create a two scores matchup was quickly extinguished as Ray Lane returned the redzone interception 92 yards for a touchdown, confirming the rout. RAYUAN LANE III PICK-SIX INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bZN2FaLptY — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Halftime Stats: Score: 28-0 Jacksonville Third Down Defense: 16.7% Jacksonville (1/6) to 66.7% Indianapolis (4/6) Defensive Sacks: 2-2 Turnovers forced: 2-1 Jacksonville Rushing yards: 118 to 42 Jacksonville Passing yards: 118 to 57 Jacksonville Redzone: 100% (1/1) Jacksonville to 0% (0/1) Indianapolis Penalties: 8 for 49-yards for Indianapolis to 3 for 25 yards Jacksonville Points off turnovers: QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half 7/11 for 138 yards and two touchdowns (146.8 passer rating), while RB Bhayshul Tuten had 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown. Following the half, Chris Rodriguez joined in on the fun with a 28 yd touchdown run to extend the third quarter lead to 35-0. Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s turn to score! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1yCUmnx74m — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Jacksonville defense took advantage of the positive game script, collecting 4.5 sacks, a fumble recovery, and two interceptions (including the previously mentioned pick six). Game balls: Special Teams: Punter Logan Cooke: 6 punts, landing 50% (3) inside the 20-yard line, and a long of 55-yards Defense: LB Foye Oluokun: 9 tackles, 5 solo, 1 sack, and 2 tackles for loss Offense: RB Bhayshul Tuten: 159 total yards, two touchdowns, and a 6.5 YPC average Pre-Game Inactives For the Jaguars: S Antonio Johnson (ankle) WR CJ Williams (healthy scratch) CB Alijah Huzzie (healthy scratch) LB Jamal Hill (healthy scratch) DE Wesley Williams (healthy scratch) DT Albert Regis (healthy scratch) For Indianapolis: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) WR Anthony Gould (concussion) CB Justin Walley (knee) TE Pharaoh Brown DT Kevin Givens OT Charlie Heck QB Riley Leonard Live blog: Recap each of the big plays from tonight’s game in our live blog ! What are your thoughts from tonight’s game, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments!

stories.title: Lions Run to Victory as Vikings’ Undefeated Streak Ends in Detroit
stories.summary: Sometimes, you need to actually score points
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 01: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings scores a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 01, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images You had to figure that, at some point, the Minnesota Vikings’ lack of offensive production would catch up with them. That’s what happened in Week 8 at Ford Field, as the Detroit Lions were able to put up enough points to end the Vikings’ undefeated streak. Jahmyr Gibbs put up yards and a touchdown, and the Minnesota offense once again failed to reach the 20-point mark as the Vikings finally fell from the ranks of the NFL’s undefeated by a score of 19-15 at Ford Field in Week 8. The Vikings got the football first after the Lions won the coin toss and chose to defer to the second half. That put Kyler Murray and company on the field right away, and they got off to a fast start as Murray found Ben Yurosek for a gain of 24 yards on the game’s first play to put the ball into Detroit territory. The drive stalled out after that, and the Vikings then called on Will Reichard to attempt a 57-yard field goal, and Reichard uncharacteristically pushed it wide to the right, leaving the Vikings empty on their opening drive. It appeared that the Lions’ first drive was going to result in a three-and-out, but the officials flagged Levi Drake Rodriguez for roughing the passer on Jared Goff to extend the drive for the Lions. But after the Vikings collected two sacks on Goff, courtesy of Andrew Van Ginkel and Eric Wilson, the Lions were forced to punt after all and the Vikings took over at their own 11. Minnesota started the next drive with Jordan Mason taking a handoff for about 10 and a first down, but that was all they could get before they called on Brett Thorson to punt it away. His boot went out of bounds at the Detroit 35 for the home team’s second possession of the afternoon. The Lions converted on a third down on a pass from Goff to Amon-Ra St. Brown despite Jalen Redmond deflecting it, and on the next third down, Goff found Jameson Williams down the seam for a big 46-yard gain. Williams was then called for a taunting penalty to push the Lions out of the red zone to the Lions’ 24-yard-line. The Lions then appeared to have a touchdown pass from Goff to St. Brown, but it was overturned on review when it was determined that St. Brown didn’t control the ball all the way through the catch. The Lions ultimately ended up settling for a field goal attempt from Jake Bates, who connected from 25 yards out to give the Lions a 3-0 lead with just over two minutes left in the first quarter. The ensuing Vikings’ possession got off to a nice start after D.J. Reed was called for pass interference on a pass to Jordan Addison to move the ball into Detroit territory at the 45-yard-line, and a few plays later Murray found the former Lion, T.J. Hockenson, for a 22-yard gain down to the Detroit 16. Aaron Jones then took a screen pass and plowed down to the 1 to make it first-and-goal, and then Justin Jefferson went and did Justin Jefferson things. . @JJettas2 is just different. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/tao9TbfnRO — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 1, 2026 The ridiculous one-handed catch gave the Vikings a 7-3 lead after the Reichard extra point less than a minute into the second quarter. Detroit’s next possession started with decent field position despite the Lions’ return man muffing the initial attempt at fielding the return. On the next third down, however, Jared Goff did something that he had not done all season before now. . .throw an interception. James Pierre picks it off! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XZ8sQnAqCx — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 James Pierre’s second interception of the year ended the Lions’ drive, but the Vikings’ offense couldn’t capitalize, and they quickly went three-and-out. Brett Thorson’s punt put the Lions at their own 8-yard line to start their next possession. The Lions picked up one first down, but ultimately punted it back to the Vikings with six and a half minutes left before halftime. The Vikings’ offense responded with an ugly three-and-out that featured Murray getting sacked, and Thorson got away a bad punt that allowed the Lions to start at midfield. The Vikings forced another Lions punt and had the ball at the two-minute warning. Murray then got out of the pocket and got the ball to near midfield, but then overthrew Jefferson on a pass and was intercepted by D.J. Reed to kill the drive. The Lions then pushed the ball into Minnesota territory and got a long carry from Gibbs to set up another field goal attempt by Bates, a 37-yarder that split the uprights to make it 7-6 going into the locker room at halftime. The Lions got the ball to start the second half, and got into Minnesota territory in just three plays, thanks largely to Gibbs. They managed to push into Minnesota territory at around the 30, but their drive stalled, and they faced a 4th-and-5 from the Minnesota 28. Bates came on for a 46-yard field goal attempt, and he bounced it off the left upright, and it fell no good, keeping the Vikings on top at 7-6 just over five minutes into the third quarter. Minnesota started their first drive of the second half with Murray getting sacked again, this time for a seven-yard loss. The drive wound up in yet another three-and-out, and the Vikings punted it away again. On the Lions’ next drive, the dam finally broke, as the Lions got into the end zone on a 30-yard touchdown run from Gibbs to put the Lions back up on top by a score of 12-7 after the two-point conversion attempt failed. The next drive saw Jordan Mason break a nice run to midfield on the first play that was called back for a hold on Will Fries. The Vikings overcame the 1st-and-20 after the hold, and converted another big third down on a seam throw from Murray to Hockenson to move into Detroit territory. After a lengthy injury timeout following an injury to Lions’ lineback Jack Campbell, the Vikings went for it on a 4th-and-5 from the Detroit 25-yard-line, and Murray’s pass for Jordan Addison fell incomplete for a turnover on downs. Detroit then quickly went three-and-out on their next possession, putting the Minnesota offense back on the field around their own 15. A few plays into the drive, the Vikings’ offense finally hit on a big play, as Murray hit Addison for a huge 51-yard gain to put the ball down at the Detroit 10-yard-line for a first-and-goal. A couple of plays later, the Vikings found the end zone again, as Murray connected with Hockenson for an 8-yard score to make it 13-12. Murray then found a wide-open Addison in the end zone for the two-point conversion to make it 15-12 with just under nine minutes left in regulation. TJ Hockenson for the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cPj2oQQZzU — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Lions’ next drive got started with a big play, as Gibbs took a handoff, reversed field, and picked up 17 yards to put the Lions near midfield. The Lions’ run game just shredded the Vikings’ defense all the way down the field and quickly found themselves with a first-and-goal from the Minnesota 7. Goff then found Jameson Williams in the back of the end zone for a 7-yard touchdown, and just like that the Lions were back on top by a score of 19-15 with four and a half minutes to go in regulation. The ensuing drive for the Vikings was a quick three-and-out, with Brett Thorson’s punt being fielded by the Lions at their own 17 with just under three minutes to play. Gibbs then broke another big run and the Lions got to the two-minute warning with a short-yardage situation. The Vikings started calling their timeouts, and eventually the Lions converted and went to victory formation, taking home the victory and handing the Vikings their first loss of the 2026 season. Kyler Murray, once again, looked awful for the most part against a Detroit defense that lost multiple starters, completing 17-of-29 passes for 210 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception. The Vikings have won games this season where they have had point totals in the teens, but this game was not one of them. It won’t get any easier for the Vikings, as they will play host to one of the AFC’s elite teams, the Buffalo Bills, on Monday Night Football next week at U.S. Bank Stadium. There are no more undefeated teams in the National Football League, as the Minnesota Vikings fall to the Detroit Lions by a score of 19-15 in Week 8 NFL action. Thank you to everyone who got their coverage of this week’s game right here at The Daily Norseman!

stories.title: Jaylen Warren rushes for 143 on his birthday, Steelers beat Browns 27-6
stories.summary: The streak continues for the Steelers and Browns in Pittsburgh.
stories.detailText: The streak continues for the Steelers and Browns in Pittsburgh. With both teams entering the contest at 5-2, Pittsburgh ran all over Cleveland to come away with a dominant 27-6 victory. The Steelers took control of the game in the first half and never really let it go, using a punishing running attack. The club had 160 yards on the ground in the first half, finishing with 201 yards in the category for the game. On his 28th birthday, Jaylen Warren led the way with 143 yards on 17 carries with a touchdown — including a 51-yard scamper. Rico Dowdle was plenty effective, too, rushing for 56 yards on 15 carries. Pat Freiermuth got into the ground game with a 1-yard tush push touchdown at the end of the first half. Aaron Rodgers wasn’t asked to do too much and did not need to, ending the game 13-of-25 for 172 yards with an interception. The pick went right off of DK Metcalf’s hands before Denzel Ward came away with it. Big tight end Darnell Washington led with three catches for 94 yards. For Cleveland, Deshaun Watson passed for over 300 yards for a second consecutive game. But he was largely stymied by the Pittsburgh defense, which produced a strip-sack on him in the first quarter that led to a touchdown. Watson finished the contest 27-of-39 for 324 yards. He was sacked eight times. Harold Fannin led with 154 yards on 10 catches. The Browns still have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003. At 6-2, the Steelers will be on their bye in Week 9. The 5-3 Browns will be on the road to face the Saints next Sunday.

stories.title: Recap: Lions grind out win with electric 2nd-half run game vs. Vikings
stories.summary: Highlight, analysis, and news from the Detroit Lions’ 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings.
stories.detailText: Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions offense looked like they had met their match in the first half against the Minnesota Vikings. But in the second half, the Lions came alive with a rushing attack that Minnesota had no answer for. The Lions dropped over 230 rushing yards on the Vikings, with impressive games from both Jahmyr Gibbs (153 yards) and Sione Vaki (65 yards). The game was stopped early in the fourth quarter when Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury and was carted to a nearby hospital. For updates on Jack Campbell injury status, click here. With the win, the Lions move to 5-2 on the season, just a game behind the no-longer-undefeated Vikings (6-1) in a tight NFC North race. First quarter The Lions won the toss and opted to defer, giving the Vikings offense the opportunity to have the ball first. After a touchback, Kyler Murray connected on a big play to put Minnesota in Lions territory on just one play. Tight end Ben Yurosek was wide open for a 24-yard gain. A deep shot to Jordan Addison went incomplete, setting up a third-and-7 from Detroit’s 38-yard line. T.J. Hockenson nearly made a diving catch, but the ball hit the ground, setting up a 57-yard attempt, and Will Reichard pushed it right for his first (non-blocked) miss of the season. Detroit took over at their own 47-yard line after the missed kick. It appeared the Lions were going to go three-and-out, but a roughing the passer penalty extended the drive after Jared Goff failed to connect with Amon-Ra St. Brown on third down. The refs would strike back in the Vikings favor, when after a first down conversion from Sione Vaki, St. Brown was called for taunting, pushing the Lions back toward midfield. Detroit wouldn’t recover, suffering sacks on two of the next three plays, pushing them out of field goal position. Pinned deep in their own zone, the Vikings managed just a single first down on a Jordan Mason 10-yard run. On the ensuing third down, Murray couldn’t find anyone open and chucked it well over Jordan Addison’s head. The Lions got a little bit of luck on their next drive, with a Goff pass deflecting into the hands of St. Brown for a ridiculous third-down conversion. Detroit nearly took full advantage. A deep shot to Jameson Williams gained 46 yards, but another taunting penalty pushed Detroit back 15 yards. Big play from Goff to JaMo on 3rd and 12! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FLspKRJxqE — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Detroit nearly found paydirt on the next play, but a 24-yard pass to St. Brown was ruled incomplete upon review when the ball was dislodged after the Lions receiver hit the ground. Amon-Ra St. Brown injury video -In locker room for concussion eval pic.twitter.com/HaWpCpZlrb — Jimmy Liao MD | Detroit Lions Morning Rounds (@JimmyLiaoMD) November 1, 2026 After the play, St. Brown was taken to the locker room, but he returned to play after the drive. Detroit was still able to move toward the goal-line, but on third-and-5, Goff, under duress, couldn’t connect with Gibbs, and they settled for a short field goal. 3-0 Lions. The Vikings offense moved to Lions territory thanks to a 23-yard pass interference penalty on D.J. Reed. Then Murray found T.J. Hockenson for 22 yards down to the 16-yard line. Second quarter The Vikings would score quickly in the second quarter, after Aaron Jones juked two defenders to turn a negative play into a 15-yard gain. Then Justin Jefferson caught a 1-yard fade to make it 7-3 Vikings 35 seconds in the quarter. Justin Jefferson. 1 of 1. MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oYt9SSvBZI — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Lions went nowhere on their next possession. After two runs went for 2 yards, Goff tried to find Williams, but the speedy receiver fell on his route, and the ball went into James Pierre’s hands for Goff’s first interception of the season. James Pierre picks it off! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XZ8sQnAqCx — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Minnesota took over at their own 46-yard line, looking to add to their lead. However, they quickly went three-and-out. Murray successful escaped pressure on third-and-9, but he airmailed a ball to Jefferson. The Vikings successfully pinned the Lions at their own 8-yard line, though, with a nice punt from Brett Thorson. Before the next drive, Lions center Cade Mays was declared questionable to return with an ankle injury. Detroit was able to overcome two early false starts, but their short-yardage run game continued to hurt them. A toss to Jahmyr Gibbs on third-and-1 was blown up in the backfield, and the Lions punted. The Vikings quickly went three-and-out thanks to a second down sack from Skyler Gill-Howard. Sun Bleach got 'em!!! pic.twitter.com/MOiNDpomQe — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 1, 2026 A shank on the punt gave the Lions the ball at midfield, but Detroit squandered the opportunity. Despite gaining 7 yards on first down, a Gibbs run went -3, and Goff was sacked for the fourth time on third down. Minnesota took over on their own 10-yard line with 3:10 left, hoping to run their two-minute drill. They kicked the drive off with a play-action boot to Jefferson for 7-yards. On the play, Brian Branch friendly-fired on defensive end DJ Wonnum, who was very slow to get up and eventually carted off. Branch also headed to the locker room, likely for a concussion evaluation. The Lions announced that both were being evaluated for concussions, and both were later downgraded to out. Murray pushed the Vikings to midfield with a scramble, but he airmailed another pass, but this time D.J. Reed picked it off. DJ Reed laid out for it and got his offense the ball back MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/crH0KuFHuV — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Lions made sure to bleed as much clock as possible to leave no time for the Vikings. But they left little time for them to realistically get in the end zone. That said, an offsides from the Vikings kept the drive alive on fourth-and-1, and Williams caught a 14-yard pass to get into field goal range. After a holding penalty pushed them back, Gibbs put them right back in with a 19-yard gain. And Jake Bates drilled it from 37 yards out to make it 7-6 Vikings at halftime. Third quarter The Lions put together a solid drive to open up the second half, mostly consisting of short passes. However, Detroit stalled on a third-down when a screen to Williams came up well short. Then Jake Bates doinked a 46-yard field goal off the left upright to keep it 7-6 Vikings. The Vikings couldn’t take advantage, as the Lions got Murray off the field with a pair of quick sacks—one by Alim McNeill and one by rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder. Detroit’s offense finally broke through on the next drive. Sam LaPorta picked up 19 yards on a checkdown to start the drive, then Gibbs started to come alive with an 11-yard run. On third-and-8, the Lions ran a neat play where St. Brown lined up about 15 yards off the line of scrimmage, then caught a pass with a running start to pick up the first. Drew Petzing borrowing from Northwestern & Chip Kelly (Tom Brady does not watch CFB) pic.twitter.com/3pYsJ1Row8 — Nick Baumgardner (@nickbaumgardner) November 1, 2026 Gibbs capped the drive with a 30-yard touchdown run, but the Lions failed the two-point conversion to move the score to 12-7 Lions. Jahmyr Gibbs races into the end zone to give the Lions the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/X42rZbve42 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Vikings looked to answer despite initially starting in a hole caused by a holding penalty forced by Tyleik Williams. A key play from Hockenson, who converted a third-and-7 with an 18-yard diving catch up the seam against Rock Ya-Sin. Detroit managed to get the Vikings into a third-and-15 from the 35-yard line, as the game moved over into the final quarter. Fourth quarter The Vikings picked up 10 yards on a pass to Hockenson, but the game came to a halt when Jack Campbell went down and appeared to go unconscious. He spent over five minutes down on the field before medical officials strapped him to a stretcher and carted him off. It was a scary scene in which the entire team came over to wish Campbell the best. Out of the long stoppage, the Vikings opted to go for it, and the Lions got the stop thanks to a pressure from Derrick Barnes and pass breakup from D.J. Reed. The Lions offense didn’t take advantage. They were able to get into a third-and-1, but a critical illegal formation on Jameson Williams negated the conversion, and Detroit would eventually punt. Minnesota would re-take the lead on their next possession thanks to a couple of big plays. Most notably, Jordan Addison got behind Khalil Dorsey and Chuck Clark for a 51-yard gain. Big play to Jordan Addison ‼️ MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KT0jWkFTdD — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Two plays later, Murray hit Hockenson for an 8-yard touchdown, and he connected with Addison on a coverage bust for the two-point conversion. 15-12 Vikings. TJ Hockenson for the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cPj2oQQZzU — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 During this drive the Lions also appeared to lose cornerback D.J. Reed to an injury. He did not come back and was announced as a hip injury. Gibbs opened the drive by reversing field for a 17-yard gain. Then Vaki took over with a 5-yard catch, a 12-yard run, and another 10 yards on the ground into field goal range. Gibbs then took over with back-to-back rushes of 9 yards down to the Vikings’ 7-yard line. Then they hit the Vikings with a play-action touchdown pass to Jameson Williams to make it 19-15 Lions with 4:35 remaining. JAMESON WILLIAMS TD MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/b87aoClNR0 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Detroit’s defense, too, answered the bell with a three-and-out. Facing a fourth-and-5 with three minutes left, the Vikings opted to trust their defense and punt the ball away. The Lions, starting on their own 17-yard line, just needed a couple of first downs to put the game away. They got one right away with a Gibbs 15-yard run on the very first play. Then he picked up another 8 yards to move the game to the two-minute warning. The Vikings, however, still had all three timeouts, so even one more first down wouldn’t clinch the game. Detroit did get another first down with a run from LaPorta. That set up a situation where they just needed one more first down. Gibbs picked up 6 yards on the first play of the new set of downs. Vaki picked up 3 on the next down. That set up a third-and-1 to clinch the game for Detroit. Goff sneaked it for the win.

stories.title: Baker Mayfield made NFL history without completing a single pass against Falcons
stories.summary: Buccaneers won an NFL game without completing a pass for the first time in 52 years
stories.detailText: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated the Atlanta Falcons by a final score of 16-0, to improve to 3-5 on the season and crawl right back into the fight at the top of the NFC South. But along the way, the Buccaneers accomplished something NFL fans have not seen since Gerald Ford was the President of the United States, back in 1974. Tampa Bay knocked off the Falcons despite not completing a single pass in the game. Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes in the game — all of those coming in the first half — and all three fell incomplete. The game began in difficult weather conditions, with a soaking rain making throwing the football extremely difficult, and as Tampa Bay held on in the second half, they leaned into the running game. Buccaneers running backs Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell combined for more than 300 yards on the ground, with Irving gaining 170 yards and Gainwell running for 133 of his own. That made the Buccaneers the sixth team in league history to win without completing a pass. The first team to pull that off was the Pittsburgh Steelers, who defeated the Brooklyn Dodgers 14-7 on November 16, 1941 despite not even attempting a pass. Pittsburgh beat Brooklyn 7-0 the following season, despite passers Bill Dudley and Andy Tomasic combining to go 0-for-7 passing. The next time a team won a game without completing a pass was again the Pittsburgh Steelers, who defeated the Chicago Cardinals 23-0 on November 11, 1945. Dudley and teammate Buss Warren combined to go 0-for-8 passing, but the Steelers won behind a pair of TD runs from Dudley, and a TD run from Warren. In 1950 the Cleveland Browns became the next team to win without completing a pass, as they knocked off the Eagles 13-7 on December 3, 1950. Cleveland did not attempt a pass that day. The last time a team won an NFL game without completing a pass? That came back in 1974, when the Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets 16-12 on September 29 of that year. Heavy rain and wind limited the passing game that day, and Bills QB Joe Ferguson went 0-for-2 passing, while Jets quarterback Joe Namath finished the game 2-for-18 for 33 yards and three interceptions. Similar to Namath in that game, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions on Sunday against Tampa Bay. Meaning the Buccaneers caught more passes from Atlanta’s quarterback in the win, than from their own.

stories.title: Cleveland Browns vs. Pittsburgh Steelers recap: Streak lives on, as Cleveland dominated and loses division lead
stories.summary: The Browns didn’t have it against the Steelers in Pittsburgh.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 1: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of a game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Browns have lost grasp of the AFC North division lead. It comes at the hands of the Pittsburgh Steelers, who made it a 23-game winning streak over Cleveland in their home stadium with a 27-6 dominant victory. It certainly wasn’t Cleveland’s day, as they turned the ball over on the first two drives, and the defense couldn’t stop Pittsburgh’s rushing attack between Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle . It looked like the Browns might keep it competitive when they added a field goal with less than a minute to go in the first half to make it 13-6, but the defense let Pittsburgh get a touchdown drive in that short span, and they basically double-dipped after the half to go up 27-6. The Browns’ offense had some opportunities, but turned it over on downs in a goal-to-go situation, and Deshaun Watson was sacked 8 times. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Steelers The Browns received the opening kickoff, and after a run by RB Quinshon Judkins , QB Deshaun Watson was sacked on second down when his quick read wasn’t there. On 3rd-and-7, Watson sailed a short pass to WR KC Concepcion for an incomplete pass, but Pittsburgh was flagged for roughing the passer for going high on Watson to give the drive new life. Watson had to exit to be checked for a concussion, bringing QB Shedeur Sanders in. Cleveland had back-to-back ineligible downfield penalties called because the Browns called simple screen passes that Pittsburgh was all over, so Sanders held the ball longer than needed. Later, on 3rd-and-13, Sanders checked it down to TE Harold Fannin to give way to P Corey Bojorquez — but then Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy threw a red challenge flag, and replay showed that the group of Steelers stripped Fannin of the ball before he was down. That gave Pittsburgh the ball at the Browns’ 42 yard line. CB Tyson Campbell knocked QB Aaron Rodgers first quick slant attempt away, as he tried to hit WR DK Metcalf . RB Jaylen Warren carried for a few yards to set up 3rd-and-7. Rodgers overshot Warren on a crossing route, so K Chris Boswell came on to try a 57-yard field goal. He missed it wide left, and ironically enough, Cleveland took over pretty quickly with better field position than where the turnover had happened at their own 47-yard line, with Watson returning. Judkins got the handoff to midfield. Then on second down, Watson was collapsed on, and then tried fumbled as he tried to throw the ball away, with Pittsburgh recovering right back at the Browns’ 45 yard line. Sack and a fumble forced by the Steelers defense 😤 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gDaB2D1rl9 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Pittsburgh fared better on their second drive, first with a swing pass to WR Germie Bernard for a first down, and then RB Rico Dowdle getting a burst of 15 yards up the middle before he was touched. A pitch play to Dowdle then went for 9 yards, setting up 2nd-and-1 at the 9 yard line. Dowdle then took it in on the next play for a 9-yard touchdown, as CB Denzel Ward tried going for the ball instead of the tackle, to put Pittsburgh up 7-0 with 7:57 to go in the opening quarter. Rico Dowdle breaking tackles on his way to the end zone! CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XuFdbhhI61 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 After the play, a personal foul penalty was called on a Steelers’ offensive lineman for extracurricular activity against DE Jared Verse , no doubt in relation to the words that were had during the week. That was enforced on the kickoff, helping WR Malachi Corley to return it out to their own 37 yard line. #Browns DE Jared Verse has been talking plenty of trash about the #Steelers …. Well, Steelers G Mason McCormick just did this to him. 😳😳 pic.twitter.com/OP1iknS4JP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 1, 2026 Watson ran a playaction on the next drive, and missed a wide open WR Denzel Boston for what would have been a 15-20-yard gain. A short connection to WR Tylan Wallace made it 3rd-and-7, and Watson was drilled from behind for the third sack of the game, and leading to a punt (which is technically better than a turnover I guess). Bojorquez’ punt was fair caught at the 11 yard line. After Warren picked up a first down on the first play, a screen play to Bernard was shut down by S Grant Delpit for a loss of 3 yards, setting up 3rd-and-13. They ran a quick-hitting run with Warren, and it was wide open up the middle and then bouncing to the outside for a gain of 51 yards, all the way to the Browns’ 25 yard line. 5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 Two plays later, another pitch out to Warren gained 8 yards to the 13 yard line for a fresh set of downs. A pass to TE Pat Freiermuth set up 3rd-and-2 at the 5 yard line. They gave it to Dowdle, who easily got 3 yards to the 2 yard line on the final play of the first quarter. 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Steelers On 1st-and-goal at the 2 yard line, a fade to Metcalf had no shot. On second down, Rodgers threw the ball away after a low snap. On third down, Rodgers handed to Warren, and the play was stuffed for no gain. The defense held strong for a big stop, as Boswell came on for a short field goal. He hit from 20 yards out to put the Steelers on top 10-0. Watson began with an 8-yard dumpoff to Fannin, and then Judkins moved the chains with a run for the team’s first first down that wasn’t via penalty. Then, on 3rd-and-7, Fannin got the ball again quickly for 12 yards and a first down to the Steelers’ 44 yard line. Off of playaction, Fannin got the catch for 25 yards to the Steelers’ 19 yard line. After a 1-yard run by Judkins, RT Tytus Howard had a false start to make it 2nd-and-14. A quick screen to Fannin gained 9 yards to set up a manageable 3rd-and-5. Watson had to throw the ball away after he couldn’t find anyone and was being hit, so K Andre Szmyt came on for a 32-yard field goal, and it was good to make it a 10-3 game with 8:43 remaining in the second quarter. Pittsburgh began their next drive at the 35 yard line. Rodgers got the Browns to bite on a fake screen, with TE Darnell Washington streaking upfield for a 24-yard gain. Then, Dowdle, after looking bottled up, broke free for 16 yards. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-3 at the 12 yard line, Rodgers handed to Dowdle for an easy first down to the 9 yard line. Like last time down here, Rodgers tried throwing the ball and had no where to go, making it second down. On second down, they tried throwing again, and it was blown up again for an incomplete pass. On third down, DT Adin Huntington got the sack for a loss of 10 yards, forcing another field goal. Boswell hit from 37 yards, to make it 13-3 with 3:27 left in the half. Adin comin' up big 💪 #CLEvsPIT on CBS pic.twitter.com/fGx5EuNluk — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 1, 2026 With the Steelers set to get the ball at the start of the second half, the offense needed another score to help draw closer. Beginning at the 25 yard line, Watson hit Boston for 5 yards, but then a false start by LG Zion Johnson made it 2nd-and-10. A run to Judkins went for 6 yards, but he had a hole and was just barely tripped up, preventing a bigger play. That made it 3rd-and-4 heading into the two-minute warning. Watson found Concepcion down the seam just before he got hit for a 24 yard gain. Boston then caught a timing pass to the outside for 12 yards, now at the Steelers 32 yard line. Watson laid one out for Boston in the end zone, just before he got hit again, but Boston couldn’t locate it and it fell incomplete. Watson got sacked by DE T.J. Watt for a loss of 8 yards on the next play, as pressure came from up the middle. On 3rd-and-18, Watson got a complete to Fannin for 9 yards to set up another field goal try by Szmyt. From 49 yards out, Szmyt was good to make it a 13-6 game with 0:45 left. The Steelers got the ball at the 31 yard line with 0:40 left and one timeout, looking to get into field goal range. Pittsburgh began with a run, and Cleveland missed a tackle as Warren got 23 yards to get close to field goal range right away. A completion in bounds was stopped for a short gain, but CB Tyson Campbell was injured, forcing Cleveland to use a timeout with 0:25 to go at the Browns’ 44 yard line. Then, Freiermuth was left uncovered in man coverage, as he picked up 27 yards to the 16 yard line. A quick screen went for 15 yards, down to the 1 yard line, and Pittsburgh clocked it with 0:05 left. Pittsburgh decided to go for it. Freiermuth lined up at quarterback, and with the tush push, they plowed into the end zone with no problem to make it 20-6 at the half, with the Steelers set to get the ball in the third quarter. Pat Freiermuth sneaks it in! CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NlChjc5Gqt — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 3rd Quarter – Browns vs. Steelers Pittsburgh began the second half with two runs to Warren to move the chains. Washington dropped an open crossing route two plays later, making it 3rd-and-5. CB Denzel Ward knocked away the third down pass for Metcalf, forcing Pittsburgh’s first punt of the game. Concepcion fair caught it at the 5 yard line, so Cleveland would begin the half backed up. Two runs by Sampson and Judkins made it 3rd-and-1. They lined up in a full house formation, and Judkins was stuffed by DT Cam Heyward for a loss of a yard, forcing a punt down to the Steelers’ 41 yard line. Cam Heyward shuts down the third and short 💪 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/c3nu0KnVIj — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Pittsburgh ran the same fake screen, downfield pass to Washington, but to the other side of the field, and it was wide open again for 58 yards down to the 1 yard line. On the next play, Warren punched it in for the touchdown to make it a 27-6 game with 9:39 left in the third quarter. BIG MAN ON THE MOVE 😤 @_Dwfootball11 pic.twitter.com/7QrUrLG0uf — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 After Cleveland got an 8-yard pass to Sampson on first down, Watson was stopped for no gain on second down, and then Watson’s third down pass was batted down by Heyward. The Browns had to punt after the three-and-out, with the Steelers taking back over at the 15 yard line. Pittsburgh moved the chains with Dowdle on 3rd-and-1 to keep another drive going. Warren had a burst up the middle on the next play for 13 yards, but as he was coming down on top of LB Carson Schwesinger , the ball came loose and Cleveland recovered. But replay review showed that Warren was down, so Pittsburgh retained possession. A few plays later, Metcalf dropped a wide open pass over the middle, and the deflection bounced right into the chest of Ward for the interception at the Steelers’ 27 yard line. RG Austin Barber was flagged for a hold on a first down run, putting Cleveland in a 1st-and-20 hole at the 17 yard line. A swing pass to Judkins got 12 yards, and then Watson hit Fannin for 16 yards and a first down. A screen pass to Judkins got 12 more yards to the Steelers’ 41 yard line. But then after the play, Judkins was flagged for taunting, making it 1st-and-10 back at the Browns’ 44 yard line again. The Browns got another first down, but a hold by LT Spencer Fano set up another 1st-and-20 on the drive, back at the 44 yard line again. Cleveland ended the quarter with a 9-yard pass to Sampson. 4th Quarter – Browns vs. Steelers On 2nd-and-11, a quick throw to Concepcion got 7 yards to make it 3rd-and-4, now likely in four-down territory. Watson found Fannin up the right sideline for a 37-yard gain, down to the 2 yard line. The give went to Judkins, but three Steelers broke through the line and Judkins was clotheslined for a loss of 3 yards. On 2nd-and-goal at the 5 yard line, Watson’s pass to Fannin was incomplete. On third down, Watson escaped a sack, rolled out, but still threw an incomplete pass. On fourth down, Watson tried to loft it over the coverage to Boston — he made a 1-hand catch, but couldn’t get his second foot in bounds, resulting in a turnover on downs. Pittsburgh faced a 3rd-and-8, and then ran it with Dowdle for a yard to force a punt. Time was not on Cleveland’s side, though, with just over 11 minutes to play — although on the plus side, it was just a 34-yard punt to the Steelers’ 42 yard line. An incomplete pass, followed by a sack for a loss of 8 yards, made it 3rd-and-18 at midfield. Watson was sacked again, and Cleveland punted with a fair catch at the 14 yard line. Pittsburgh moved the ball a little before punting to the 13 yard line themselves. Fannin’s big receiving day continued with catches of 27 and 10 yards to midfield. A few plays later, it was 3rd-and-16 from the 30 yard line, and Watson’s pass was tipped and incomplete. On fourth down, they had to go for it, and Watson just dumped it off to TE Blake Whiteheart for a turnover on downs. Cleveland’s run defense forces losses of 6, 3, and 1 yard on the next three plays, with QB Mason Rudolph at quarterback now, as Pittsburgh punted inside of two minutes. Concepcion returned the punt 22 yards to the Steelers’ 44 yard line. After three completions to Sampson, and then a throw to Boston at the 1 yard line, the Browns called their final timeout. They tried running it with Judkins, but it was stopped, and then Cleveland couldn’t get another play off, ending the game with no points. Quick Hitters QB Deshaun Watson: 27-of-39 for 324 yards TE Harold Fannin: 10 catches, 154 yards The Browns have to re-group and take advantage of their ‘easy’ schedule still to come. Also helping is the fact that the Ravens lost, and lost their top two quarterbacks. The Bengals are also losing to the Titans as of the finish to the Browns game, which means Cleveland could still be in second place in the division and in line for a wildcard spot. Up next, the Browns stay on the road to take on the New Orleans Saints.

stories.title: Lions rally late to knock off Kyler Murray and the Vikings, the NFL's last undefeated team
stories.summary: The Lions flew ahead in the second half to beat the Vikings 19-15 at home on Sunday afternoon, even after losing linebacker Jack Campbell to a scary neck injury.
stories.detailText: The Minnesota Vikings' undefeated run has come to an end. Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions rallied late after losing star linebacker Jack Campbell to a scary neck injury to knock off the NFL's last undefeated team on Sunday afternoon at Ford Field. They picked up a 19-15 win over the Vikings, ending Minnesota's six-game win streak to open the 2026 campaign. Despite their perfect record, the Vikings have struggled in recent weeks — especially offensively. They only snuck past the Indianapolis Colts last week late to maintain their undefeated streak . And for much of Sunday's contest, those struggles continued. The Vikings entered halftime up by just a single point after what was a slow start from Kyler Murray. He went just 7 of 15 for 86 yards in the opening half, and threw a pretty bad interception while trying to force a throw just before the break. That set up a late Lions field goal. DJ Reed diving INT! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wBC8wCugnN — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Now, Detroit wasn't much better. Quarterback Jared Goff threw his first interception of the season in the first half, and they missed a field goal on their opening drive of the third quarter. Finally, though Jahmyr Gibbs broke open a 30-yard run late in the third period to give the Lions their first lead of the afternoon. To Murray's credit, he had his moments. He found Justin Jefferson for a 1-yard touchdown in the second quarter to get them on the board, and then he set up a touchdown pass to TJ Hockenson and a 2-point conversion with a wild 51-yard pass to Jordan Addison. Big play to Jordan Addison ‼️ MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KT0jWkFTdD — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 That didn't hold. Goff, after a few big gains from Gibbs, found a wide open Jameson Williams for a touchdown to put them in front by four with just 4:35 left. The Minnesota defense, which has been solid all season, had no answers on that drive. JAMESON WILLIAMS TD MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/b87aoClNR0 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Vikings went three-and-out after that, and Murray again tried to force a ball deep to Addison on third down. They opted to punt, and the Lions simply rode out the four-point win. Goff went 18 of 25 for 176 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the win for the Lions, which pushed them to 5-2 on the season. They've won three straight now, too. Gibbs had 153 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries, which marked his third game this season with at least 150 yards on the ground. Williams finished with 70 yards and a score on four catches. Campbell went down early in the fourth quarter while trying to make a tackle, and had to be loaded onto a stretcher and taken off the field. Several Lions players were extremely emotional, and defensive captain Aidan Hutchinson appeared to be crying. Campbell was transported to a local hospital with a neck injury. Murray finished 17 of 29 for 210 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the loss for Minnesota. He was the team's leading rusher with 35 yards on four carries. Addison ended with 66 yards on three catches. While they've now lost, the Vikings are still in great position in the NFC North race. They've only won the division once in the past nine seasons, most recently in 2022. Now, they'll have to bounce back against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills next week, which won't be an easy task. And their offensive inconsistency is still an issue they need to address if they are going to claim a division title and live up to their hot start. How Murray and the Vikings bounce back over the next week will be key to how things go down the stretch.

stories.title: Josh Allen overtakes Jim Kelly for most touchdown passes in Bills history
stories.summary: Allen overtook Hall of Famer Jim Kelly for most career passing touchdowns by a Buffalo Bill in Week 8.
stories.detailText: Josh Allen became the Buffalo Bills' all-time leader in touchdown passes in Sunday's matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. With 259 career touchdown passes, Allen passed Bills legend and Hall of Famer Jim Kelly in combined regular-season and postseason scoring passes. He reached the mark in 150 games, while Kelly got his 258 touchdown passes in 177 career appearances. Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Kelly is still on top of the franchise's all-time list in touchdown passes thrown during the regular season with 237. But Allen is closing in with 230 after his 11-yard passing touchdown to wide receiver DJ Moore in Week 8, extending their lead to 29-10. It’s the second time the pair have connected for a touchdown since the Bills acquired Moore via a trade with the Chicago Bears back in March. Buffalo has 10 more games on the 2026-27 schedule and also has the remainder of Week 8's contest versus Baltimore. The Hall of Famer also has 17 postseason touchdown passes compared to Allen's 15. stories.summary: Atlanta endures the worst loss of the season and one of the worst losses you can endure in Week 8.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We hoped and prayed the Falcons would buck a seemingly ancient trend of falling down after a major win against a contender, and we hoped and prayed in vain. Our favorite team went to Tampa Bay in a downpour that turned into a drizzle and washed away their hopes of taking possession of the NFC South lead with an embarrassing effort that undermined almost every positive the Falcons have put forth in recent weeks. Let’s be honest about what we saw Sunday: It was an ass kicking where Atlanta was entirely out-coached, out-played, and out-hustled. Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass, yet the Buccaneers didn’t care because they ran for 300 yards. The Falcons had Bijan Robinson, but somehow that didn’t matter because the Falcons got down after throwing too much and then started throwing nonstop late. The Falcons were within striking distance—or at least not dead—all day, but yet could not turn in a single point. There is nothing that can be said about the caliber of performance the Falcons put on the field today that is positive, and aside from a handful of strong individual performances, Atlanta was humiliated and humbled by their rival. Now 3-5, the Falcons are back down with the Buccaneers and the division is a muddle, and Atlanta’s highs are matched by their lows as they continue to be defined by inconsistency and utterly baffling performances after stunningly good ones. This loss is impossible to justify and tough to swallow, and this is the kind of doubt-sprouting performance that the Falcons will now be combating the rest of the year. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. I suggest not bothering to read it, but thanks for stopping by. 1st Quarter Bijan picked up three yards on first down, then Michael Penix Jr. hit Jahan Dotson for 19 yards. Bijan then went two yards and then was stalled for no gain, and Penix couldn’t connect with Drake London. In the rain from 53 yards, Nick Folk’s field goal attempt went wide left. The Buccaneers took over near midfield, and then Bucky Irving took it almost 20 yards. Irving got a yard on first down. After three yards, Kendal Daniels got Irving out of bounds. Baker Mayfield then bombed it downfield and threw it a bit behind his receiver, who had it knocked loose by Mike Hughes, who arrived with excellent timing. Chase McLaughlin’s field goal try was good to make it 3-0 Buccaneers. Zachariah Branch took it to about the 28, and an illegal formation call on the Buccaneers gave Atlanta five more yards. On the next play, Penix simply missed the defender and threw an interception right to him, with Drake London picking up a 15 yard penalty for unnecessary roughness on the same play. Buccaneers ball. Irving took it five yards on first down. Then in a wildly bewildering sequence, Baker Mayfield got out of a busted situation, scrambled, flipped the ball to Bucky Irving, and Irving was galloping toward the end zone…only to have Jessie Bates come in and chop the ball out of his hands, where it landed out of bounds in the end zone. Falcons ball! Bijan Robinson got called for a first down, and then picked up five yards. Penix didn’t see anything downfield on second down, and tried the outlet to Bijan, who dropped it. Then Penix threw another interception, again to Anzalone. Buccaneers ball. Irving was stopped for a loss by Brandon Dorlus. Irving then got three yards. Mayfield missed badly on third down, setting up a McLaughlin field goal. 6-0 Buccaneers. Branch slid down past the 25 yard line. Bijan then took it for four yards. Bijan then cut it inside for another four. Penix evaded the pressure, but wildly overthrew Pitts. The Jake Bailey punt rolled to the 13 yard line. Bucky Irving then picked up 12 yards on first down. Baker fumbled the snap and handed it to Irving, who got a yard. Irving then got a couple more yards on second down. Gainwell was then quickly tackled after maybe a yard. 2nd Quarter Dotson called for a fair catch on the Falcons 39 yard line. Bijan then appeared to run into the pile for a minimal gain, but emerged on the other side for almost 15 yards. Then he picked up two yards. Penix then made a dangerous arcing throw to Dotson, who had it bounce off his hands. Khalil Herbert then ran into the pile for maybe a yard. Irving then picked up another five yards. Irivng was tripped up by Daniels for another four yards. Irving got another first down and five yards, and followed that up with six yards. Gainwell then took it almost 20 yards. Gainwell went up the middle for a yard or two. A false start on the Bucs backed them up five yards. A one yard gain by Bijan gave way to a nice, physical run where he picked up nine yards and a first down. Herbert then picked up two yards. Penix then sort of threw it away to the sideline in the direction of a receiver. Bijan somehow then managed to bully his way to a first down on 3rd and 8, but on booth review he was ruled down after a six yard gain. On fourth down, they gave it to Bijan, who came up a little short of a conversion. Bucs ball. Irving then rolled for 13 yards on first down. C.J. Henderson then got Irving after a couple of yards. stories.title: Who is Joe Fagnano? Meet the Ravens emergency QB after Jackson, Huntley injuries
stories.summary: Joe Fagnano likely wasn't expecting to play in Week 8, but he did. Here's what to know about the Ravens emergency QB.
stories.detailText: New character unlocked. Week 8 of the NFL season saw the debut of a new quarterback, Joe Fagnano. An undrafted rookie out of UConn, Fagnano was forced into action as the Baltimore Ravens emergency quarterback following injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. And it was Fagnano's first snaps in the pros, outside of the preseason action he participated in over the summer. In other words, "Spooky Season" was granted an extension into November this year. The Ravens have dealt with quarterback issues before, but never to this extent. To put it in perspective, Baltimore is one injury to Fagnano away from playing backup running back Justice Hill at quarterback. Here's what to know about Fagnano. Who is Joe Fagnano? Fagnano is an undrafted rookie quarterback for the Baltimore Ravens . The 25-year-old grew up in Williamsport, Pennsylvania – a place best known for being the birthplace of Little League Baseball. Fagnano eventually earned a scholarship at the University of Maine after arriving as a walk-on, appearing in 27 games over four seasons. Fagnano transferred to UConn ahead of the 2023 season and appeared in 24 games during his three seasons with the Huskies. He entered the 2026 NFL Draft, but went undrafted and signed with the Ravens – along with Vanderbilt's Diego Pavia. Fagnano ended up securing the third string job during training camp and prompting Baltimore to move on from Pavia, who is now set to join the UFL . Was Joe Fagnano drafted? Fagnano was not drafted during the 2026 NFL Draft. Joe Fagnano college stats Fagnano played 27 games and started 25 in four seasons at the FCS level with the Maine Black Bears. He finished his FCS career with a 10-15 record, completed 59.8% of passes for 5,674 passing yards, 46 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. Fagnano added 535 rushing yards and five touchdowns as a runner during that time as well. Following his transfer to UConn, Fagnano made 20 starts and appeared in 24 games. He posted a 13-6 record, completed 64.7% of passes and threw for 5,252 yards, 48 touchdowns and six interceptions. Just like at Maine, Fagnano used his legs to total 223 rushing yards and four touchdowns. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Who is Joe Fagnano? stories.title: Daniel Jones benched after another rough performance in blowout vs. Jaguars
stories.summary: Anthony Richardson was called upon in the fourth quarter in Week 8.
stories.detailText: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones entered Week 8 with questions already swirling about his job security . While head coach Shane Steichen offered a vote of confidence for his quarterback prior to Sunday's game, it didn't take long for Jones to make his coach regret that decision. After throwing two interceptions in a blowout, Jones was benched in favor of Anthony Richardson Sr. against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It marked the first time Richardson saw game action since Week 5 of last season. The Colts made the switch with a little over 11 minutes to play in the contest. At the time he was replaced, Jones was 19 for 28 with 144 yards and a touchdown. He also threw two interceptions in the contest, one of which was returned for a Jaguars' score to put the team up 28-0 at halftime. Despite that first interception, Jones opened the third quarter as the Colts' starter. He made it through the third quarter, even tossing a touchdown to prevent a shutout. But on his first drive of the fourth quarter, Jones was picked off by Branson Combs, ending the quarterback's day. It's been a rough season for Jones after a breakout 2025. Heading into Week 8, the quarterback had just four passing touchdowns against seven interceptions in seven starts. Last year, Jones threw 19 touchdowns in 13 starts before a torn Achilles prematurely ended his season. The Colts were 8-5 at the time of Jones' injury. The team went 0-5 over its final five games, falling out of the playoffs. While there were questions about Jones' availability throughout training camp, the quarterback was able to recover in time to start for the Colts in Week 1. But through seven games, Jones hasn't recaptured last season's success. After getting benched in Week 8, it could signal the end of Jones' tenure in Indianapolis. Though the team signed Jones to a significant extension that carries the quarterback through 2028, the team can get out of that deal this offseason. Following his benching Sunday, that seems like the likeliest outcome now. This story will be updated.

stories.title: Buccaneers don't complete a pass, beat Falcons 16-0 anyway
stories.summary: In one of the most shocking box scores you'll ever see, the Bucs won without completing a pass in rainy Tampa Bay.
stories.detailText: The Buccaneers did something today that hadn't been done in the NFL in more than half a century: They played an entire game without completing a pass. Amazingly, the Buccaneers beat the Falcons anyway. Baker Mayfield was 0-for-3 passing, but Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell both had more than 100 yards rushing, and the Buccaneers won 16-0 on a rainy, sloppy day in Tampa Bay. The last NFL team to play an entire game without completing a pass was the 1974 Bills, who also won when they did it, beating the Jets 16-12 on a day when O.J. Simpson ran for 117 yards. The Buccaneers were helped by an ugly game from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix, who went 8-for-24 for 125 yards, with no touchdowns and four interceptions. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson struggled to get his footing in the bad weather and finished with 76 yards on 19 carries. The game leaves both the Buccaneers and the Falcons at 3-5 on the season, and both in the mix in the wide-open NFC South. If the Buccaneers' defense and running game can keep playing like they did today, the Bucs may be a playoff team. But they're going to need Mayfield to complete some passes.

teamStories.title: Jets waste offensive outburst in costly 38-33 loss to Raiders
teamStories.summary: The Jets' offense erupted for 33 points, but defensive breakdowns and a costly kickoff return helped the Raiders secure a 38-33 win at MetLife Stadium.
teamStories.detailText: The Jets had their best offensive performance in some time on Sunday, but it wasn’t enough as their defense and special teams unit failed to hold up their end of the bargain. In addition, when the offense had a chance to take a late lead, it came up short once again as the Las Vegas Raiders held on for a 38-33 win at MetLife Stadium. New York took an early lead on a short field goal by Jason Sanders , but the Raiders drove downfield on their first possession to take a 7-3 lead on a Kirk Cousins 12-yard pass to Brock Bowers . After another Jets field goal, they got the ball back and took a 13-7 lead on Geno Smith ’s 18-yard pass to Isaiah Williams , but the Raiders retook the lead immediately as Dylan Laube returned the ensuring kickoff 95 yards for a score. The Jets scored twice more before halftime to lead 23-14 as Smith threw another touchdown pass to Adonai Mitchell , then New York kicked a field goal just before half time. Prior to that kick, the Jets had been outscored 107-6 in the last two minutes of the first half during the Aaron Glenn era. The Raiders soon got back into the game, as Cousins wrapped up another good drive with a two-yard pass to Bowers. The Jets responded immediately though, scoring on their next possession on a Braelon Allen 21-yard run. Las Vegas once again scored a touchdown on their next drive as Cousins’ 1-yard run made it a 30-28 game. Then, having forced the Jets to punt for the first time all day, they took a 35-30 lead with 11:33 to go on Cousins’ 2-yard pass to Jalen Nailor . The Jets got back into the red zone with under five minutes left, but their drive stalled yet again, so Sanders made another field goal to cut the Raiders’ lead to 35-33 with 4:31 remaining. However, the defense’s inability to get a stop cost the Jets once again and Las Vegas were able to run out most of the rest the clock. Matt Gay ’s 53-yard field goal made it a five-point game with 27 seconds remaining. Smith’s Hail Mary pass was intercepted in the end zone by Jeremy Chinn to clinch the Raiders’ win with seven seconds remaining. Here are the key takeaways… - The Jets got off to a terrific start, as they were inside the Raiders’ 5-yard line just three plays into the game. However, some of the issues that have been blighting them in recent weeks immediately resurfaced as the drive stalled and they had to settle for a field goal. After the Raiders’ first touchdown, the Jets again got into the red zone but again ended up with just a field goal. - New York stayed aggressive, though, taking advantage of a Las Vegas defense which is statistically one of the worst in the NFL. The Jets scored on each of their first six possessions, including on a couple of red-zone touchdown passes by Smith, who had 146 passing yards by halftime. However, the Jets completely lost their momentum in the second half. - It wasn’t just the passing game that was working for the Jets because Allen’s recent great play continued as he had 121 rushing yards by halftime, then went in untouched from 21 yards out early in the second half. He ended up with just 147 yards, though, as the Jets had less success running the ball after halftime. - Despite the offensive success, the defense struggled all day. The defensive line was always going to be shorthanded without T’Vondre Sweat and David Bailey , although Will McDonald had a big third down sack in the first half to force a rare punt. - The Jets made a concerted effort to get Garrett Wilson involved this week, going to him often in the first half, including on a 31-yard pass on the very first play of the game. Mitchell also had a big game going up against Eric Stokes as he racked up a career-high 142 yards on seven catches. Wilson ended up with six catches for 83 yards, but his longest catch of the day was negated by a penalty. - The Jets’ rookies, Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq , were hardly involved in the game plan, though, which goes to show how difficult it is to involve everyone. Following back-to-back 100-yard games, Cooper wasn’t even targeted, although Sadiq did have a spectacular leaping catch in the second half. - For all his big talk during the week, Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty was mostly a nonfactor as Las Vegas featured rookie Mike Washington more heavily instead. Jeanty had just one carry for one yard entering the fourth quarter. However, his 45-yard catch and run set up a go-ahead score in the fourth quarter. Game MVP: Raiders QB Kirk Cousins In the matchup of two quarterbacks who are well into their thirties, it was Cousins whose team got the win as he passed for 247 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing for a touchdown. teamStories.summary: Jets’ defense putrid in latest defeat
teamStories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 1: Dylan Laube #23 of the Las Vegas Raiders returns a kick off for a touchdown against the New York Jets in the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on November 1, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ eighth game of the 2026 season, on a gorgeous, warm and sunny day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets lost to the Las Vegas Raiders, 38 – 33. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They got off to an explosive start. A long completion to Garrett Wilson and two long runs by Braelon Allen got the Jets a first and goal at the Raiders two yard line. From there the Jets bogged down, as they never gained another yard. The Jets settled for a short field goal and an early 3 – 0 lead. The lead didn’t last. The Raiders marched right down the field against a Jets defense providing only token resistance. The drive ended when Kirk Cousins found Brock Bowers in the end zone, inexplicably being covered by Travis Brownlee. That matchup went about as you might expect. Touchdown, Raiders. The Raiders had a 7 – 3 lead midway through the first quarter. The Jets answered by grinding out a long drive before settling for a short field goal. At this point the Jets had scored on their first two drives and still trailed 7 – 6 late in the first quarter. The first quarter ended with the Raiders punting after a three and out and the score still Raiders 7, Jets 6. The Jets proceeded to take the ball down the field, with multiple connections to Adonai Mitchell. The drive ended when Geno Smith found Isaiah Williams in the end zone for a touchdown and a 13 – 7 Jets lead early in the second quarter. The Jets lead lasted about 15 seconds. Dylan Laube returned the ensuing kickoff for a touchdown and just like that the Jets trailed the Raiders, 14 – 13. The lead changed hands again shortly thereafter. The Jets drove right down the field. Braelon Allen had a big run and Geno Smith eventually found Adonai Mitchell in the end zone for a touchdown and a 20 – 14 Jets lead midway through the second quarter. Thus far neither defense looked like they had any intention of providing a challenge for the opposing offense. The Jets defense stopped the Raiders on fourth down and the Jets offense took over for what they hoped would be the final drive of the first half. Braelon Allen ran the ball down the Raiders’ throats. Then a miracle happened. With just a few seconds left in the first half the Jets kicked a short field goal. A rare Jets score in the final two minutes of the half closed out the first half scoring. The Jets went into the locker room leading the Raiders 23 – 14, having scored on every drive of the half. The Jets opened the third quarter on defense. It did not go well. The Raiders went right down the field, mixing runs and passes effectively. Eventually Kirk Cousins found Brock Bowers for his second touchdown of the game as both teams continued to play only token defense. The score was now Jets 23, Raiders 21 early in the third quarter. It didn’t take long for the Raiders’ defense to give the touchdown back. After Isaiah Williams returned the kickoff out to the 42 yard line, the Jets moved swiftly down the field. A completion to Garrett Wilson, a completion to Kenyon Sadiq, and a long run by Braelon Allen put the Jets in the end zone. It was the sixth consecutive Jets drive ending in a score. The extra point gave the Jets a 30 – 21 lead midway through the third quarter. It was the first time the Jets scored more than 25 points this season. The Raiders came back. Kirk Cousins marched them down the field and eventually ran it in himself for a touchdown. The shootout was on as the score was now Jets 30, Raiders 28 late in the third quarter. A Jets holding penalty followed by a sack of Geno Smith resulted in the first Jets drive all game that did not end in a score. The Jets punted and the Raiders got the ball with a chance to take the lead in the closing minutes of the third quarter. As the quarter ended the Raiders were close to midfield, moving the ball towards what threatened to be a go ahead score. Ashton Jeanty broke off a big catch and run. A few plays later the Raiders were in the end zone with their third straight touchdown on three second half possessions. That gave the Raiders a 35 – 30 lead early in the fourth quarter as the Jets defense continued to come up small. After the two teams traded three and outs the Jets got the ball. The Raiders had them bottled up with a third and forever, but they bailed the Jets out with a defensive holding penalty. With a new lease on life Geno Smith completed a gorgeous bomb to Adonai Mitchell to give the Jets a first down inside the Raiders’ 15 yard line. Unfortunately the Jets drive stalled from there. The Jets had to settle for a short field goal, making the score Raiders 35, Jets 33 with a little more than four minutes left in the game. On the ensuing possession the Raiders used up all but 27 seconds left in the game on a drive ending in a long field goal, giving them a 38 – 33 lead with 27 seconds left and the Jets out of timeouts. The Jets got to the Raiders 35 yard line before Geno Smith was intecepted in the end zone on a last gasp heave, effectively ending the game. Final score: Raiders 38, Jets 33. The loss brought the Jets’ record to 2-6. Another year of playing out the string for the last two months of the season awaits. The Jets go on the road next week to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. It will be shocking if the Jets are competitive in that game.
