teamStories.title: Raiders end losing streak with 38-33 win over Jets
teamStories.summary: Kirk Cousins threw three touchdowns to get the Raiders to 4-4 on the year.
teamStories.detailText: The Dolphins picked up their first win of the 2026 season against the Jets at MetLife Stadium in Week 7 and the Raiders found it to be a hospitable place to play in Week 8. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdowns and ran for another as the Raiders ended their four-game losing streak with a 38-33 win over the Jets. The victory bumps their record to 4-4 ahead of a Week 9 trip to face the 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Cousins's third touchdown pass of the day went to Jalen Nailor with 11:33 left to play in the game and it put the Raiders up 35-30 after they trailed by nine points at halftime. They allowed the Jets to drive the ball to their 13, but their defense was able to come up with a stop that led to Jason Sanders's fourth field goal of the day. Raiders running back Mike Washington ran for one first down and the Jets used all their timeouts before a Cousins sneak on third down gave them another one at the two minute warning. The Jets were able to stop the Raiders on the next third down and Matt Gay hit a 53-yard field goal with 27 seconds left to play. The Jets got the ball back and a penalty on a Garrett Wilson catch got them into Raiders territory, but Smith chucked one into the end zone from the 35-yard-line and it was picked off by Jeremy Chinn to the end the game. Sanders's first two kicks also came on Jets drives that got the ball into the red zone and the failure to score touchdowns haunted the Jets a day after Halloween. They churned up 424 yards and scored on their first six possessions, but settling for field goals and a defense that lived down to Ashton Jeanty's slam of them got them beat on Sunday. Jeanty was little more than a third-down back for the Raiders, but he did have a 45-yard catch to set up one touchdown. Washington ran 25 times for 83 yards and the Brock Bowers/Michael Mayer tight end combo had 12 catches for 145 yards. Two of Bowers's catches went for touchdowns and Cousins was 19-of-26 for 247 yards on the afternoon. The Raiders scored on six of their nine full possessions and they also got a 95-yard kickoff return from Dylan Laube on their way to the win. The Jets' defensive shortcomings crushed them on a day when Braelon Allen, Adonai Mitchell, and Garrett Wilson all had big days against an overmatched Raiders defense. There's a lot to like about the amount of talent on the offensive side of the ball for the Jets, but Aaron Glenn's defensive acumen is creating no reason to believe he's the right man for the job. The Jets fell to 2-6 with the loss and they will be in Kansas City next Sunday.

teamStories.title: Rex Ryan rips Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty, who takes backseat role against Jets
teamStories.summary: ESPN analyst Rex Ryan, a former Jets head coach, ripped Las Vegas Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty, who issued bulletin-board material before facing New York.
teamStories.detailText: The lack of production from the Las Vegas Raiders ' run game during the 2026 season falls on the entire offensive unit and first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, along with his staff. But the rushing woes have magnified the plight of one specific player: Raiders' running back Ashton Jeanty, in his second season of pro ball after Las Vegas selected him sixth overall in the 2025 draft. The Raiders (3-4) entered the Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets ranked 31st in rushing yards per game (74.7) and 31st in yards per rush, a category they were also ranked last in a season ago). The Raiders handed center Tyler Linderbaum the richest contract in the history of the position (three years, $81 million) to help bolster a lackluster offensive line. Jeanty was averaging 3.1 yards per carry entering the game against the Jets – down from his rookie-year mark of 3.7. However, Jeanty saw the matchup as an opportunity to get the run game back on track, however. He also took a shot at the Jets defense in the process. "I think we can definitely get the run game going," Jeanty told reporters . "Get back on track. … A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names." Former Jets head coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan took plenty of offense to the comments and aired his grievances on "Sunday NFL Coundown." "Why? Because you are horrible. You're about the worst draft pick of the last 20 years, I think, as a running back," Ryan said. "You stink. You're averaging 3.1 yards per carry. ... It's on you, my friend. "This kid right here? He's not as good as the backup. And he's running his mouth? They've lost four games in a row. They haven't won in a month and he's running his mouth." Rex Ryan on Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty saying that there are a couple of Jets who look like they don’t want to tackle: pic.twitter.com/zoXmTnwQpK — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 Jeanty's comments may not have sat well within his own locker room. He had one carry in the first half (for one yard) and caught one pass. Running back Mike Washington carried seven times for 24 yards in the first half as the Raiders trailed the Jets.
